This is my first Rising Storm game and I have never played a game from the developers until today. I joined a match in progress as the Viet Cong, we lost, but it was a lot of fun. I'll list some positives and negatives of the game...
Positives
- The realism in this game is thick, and it is a breath of fresh air. I had made a post about how I was coming from COD WW2 and would like something more realistic, different era, etc. Hardcore mode in CoD is not hardcore compared to the normal mode of this game, and that is quite alright. They focus on two different gameplay styles. You can't whip grenades halfway across a map and you can't wait for your gun to automatically reload when you go dry. This game is realistic af.
- The communications actually work quite well. I did not play the role of a radioman, but I was hearing the commander give orders, guidance, etc. and I could understand him easily. No one was yelling obscenities or anything about anyone's mother, although I can ony assume my game was a rarity in that aspect. lol Correct me if I'm wrong!
- When you die, you don't get a killcam. This would irk the living hell out of a lot of players but I find it refreshing. I don't feel the need to go find that guy and kill him, I don't even know what he looks like. Another feature I liked is that you can apologize with a key press if you teamkill someone or get teamkilled. I shot a few of my fellow charlie and I liked the option to apologize.
- Teamwork really is key. Mostly, one shot and you're dead. In the game I was in, I didn't see any Rambo situations and that's ok. That isn't what war is like anyway.
- There seems to be a wide variety of weapons and classes available which is awesome. Customizing is something I love to do.
Negatives
- The graphics are a bit dated but that is completely understandable, this isn't some triple A lootbox infested beautiful art gallery. It's gritty and being shot in the head leads to a black screen, which I can only assume is what it is like being shot in the head. lol
Honestly, that was all I got from my first game. Most of the shots that I fired and I feel like should've hit I knew that I was probably just off, the aiming is a lot more realistic as well.
Overall, what was going to be a 'hey let's try this game out online for 5 mins and go eat breakfast' turned into a 'GET IN THE TUNNELS, THEY'RE TAKING B!' or some sneaky Viet Cong jungle stuff. It was awesome. I recommend the game.

Copoka really is unique, and that in many ways.
The ability to play as a bird and freeroam in the skies or on the ground was the main reason I've decided to give it a shot, but there is a bit more to this game than just flying around and experiencing a city from a bird's perspective. However, at the same time, not too much more either. That is not to say the game doesn't offer a lot for its price, ultimately.
Make no mistake, this game is more of a laidback "zen session" than an actual game in the classic sense, something you want to beat. Sure, there are goals. There are "collectibles" and "upgrades". But I do not believe these are the things you necessarily want to exclusive go after when playing.
Your goal is to find various objects in this world to add to your nest and enhance it, so called "trinkets", such as a broken glasses frame or a bottleneck. Trinkets will be highlighted and are rather easily visible when you're high up and looking around. Having picked up a trinket, your nest will be marked in yellow and enables you to easily find your way back. Once you have collected 5 trinkets, you will progress to the next "set" of trinkets to collect. And with that, you will progress in the story.
Yes, a story, and I will come to this later.
While collecting the trinkets you can also collect up to 11 feathers which will permanently upgrade your speed to actually significant levels. I have only collected 2 or 3 feathers in my playtime and felt a nice increase. Soaring through the sky is a lot more fun with a few speed upgrades, that I will definitely say.
The aesthetic is very intriguing, reminding me a bit of Mirror's Edge in the sense that most buildings are very simplistic, boring even, and colored in white. In stark contrast to that, however, is the lush environment around with colors of all sorts. Your bird is rather realistic-looking, too, in very stark contrast to the humans, which coupled with the nice animations while flying really adds to the sense of surreality. And then, of course, you have really beautiful music playing along, which can just as well be abruptly interrupted by military chanting over extremely loud speakers as you get close to the city hall.
It should be evident that this game is all about drawing you into a totalitarian world, beautiful to a bird when looked at from the sky, but horrible when on the ground and close to sick and fearful humans. You do have a choice which of these you want to experience, though, and this is a very good thing. You are a bird, after all. You can fly anywhere you want.
Finally, there is indeed even a story of sorts involved. A story which might very well come as expected from a game that features such a totalitarian state. But also one that might very well surprise you. It certainly did surprise me, and I felt compelled to listen closely and observe the changes the lands were going through.
Yet, as I mentioned above, it is not forced upon you. That is a really good thing, and now that I have "beaten" the game after about an hour, I honestly want to do a second playthrough at some point where I will try to listen to every conversation. Surprisingly enough, it should be noted, the voice acting is actually not terrible. It isn't even bad. It's... quite decent, at times good even. Though I suppose that goes to show there is a good amount of love in this project.
If that sounds interesting to you, then yes, by all means, support this little indie product. It offers on point value/money right now, and I can only hope that a few more additions and improvements will be made in the future. If not, hell, it's still a really neat little game.
__________
Speaking of improvements, here are a few things I would like to criticize in hope that they will be improved:
Performance seems to be fairly decent on my system (Max/"Beautiful" graphics at 1080p). I run a 4.6GHz i7-6700k, 16GB of high-speed DDR4 RAM and an overclocked GTX 970, outputting to a 72Hz monitor.
However, despite the game being locked to 60fps, it cannot always maintain this and drops to around 45-40fps at times, though chances are you will not notice this all too much, as the game otherwise runs smoothly and is relatively chill and relaxed in the first place. Regardless, this is a bit weird, as it seems to run in the Unreal Engine and certainly does not offer the graphical fidelity to justify those drops.
But, keep in mind, it's not outright terrible to begin with. The game clearly works well, for the biggest part, which is why I am only mentioning this to point out the room and need for improvement, but also to make potential buyers who want their performance to be rock-solid and completely stable aware of it. If you are such a person, you might want to wait a bit.
Other than performance, the interface needs a little bit of polish, in my opinion. While you are able to choose between a standard and a more snappy control method, rebindable buttons and keys would be nice. Now, I chose the snappy control method, as it offers nice and pretty responsive control over your bird. But, despite the game claiming you will be able to change this at any time, you cannot actually do so without starting a new game. Either that or I'm really oblivious, but I haven't been able to find such an option anywhere else but at the start of a new game.
Lastly, I feel like the tutorial should be a tiny little bit more helpful. It will teach you how to take off, accelerate and break, but that is pretty much it. You could argue that this really is all you need, and I agree to some extent, but there are three more buttons bound. One you hold down to teleport back to your nest, and the other two for doing a birdcall. But I do not know if doing a birdcall actually does anything useful.
All of these things are, in my opinion, rather minor but should be noted regardless.
__________

Its a group based, real time RPG/hack&slay with different class systems.

Fitst Time ever playing this:
Pros: Beautiful artwork
Entertaining characters and dialogue
Engaging story
Cons:
Cumbersome interface and interaction system makes doing thing more complicated and harder than they need to be.
Puzzles can be overly complicated, vague, or simply arbitrary.
Examples (also spoilers):
For one puzzle, you have to give a troll something appealing, but invaluable, so he will let you pass. This thing is a red Herring, which makes little sense given the meaning of a Red Harring(a useless/misleading clue). I guess it's an incredibly meta joke about how you have a literal Red Herring in a puzzle game that must be given to a troll that wants something useless, but appealing, but that's a pretty obscure reference for someone to figure out, and actually contradicts itself because if the red herring is used to solve a puzzle, it's useful, and it's not exactly useless is it?
But that's not the main problem. The big problem I find is that in order to get the herring, you have to scare away a seagull, and to do that, you have to step on a plank multiple times to launch it into the air. However, the plank looks no different than any other part of the floorboard, and must be stepped on in a specific part to activate, so how is anyone supposed to figure out they need to step on a plank that has no indication of being loose (or interactable for that matter) in order to scare the bird away?
Another puzzle that I couln't figure out without help was with finding the swordmaster. Now I didn't need help because I couldn't figure out what to do. I needed help because the game failed(by some program problem) so make it possible to solve the puzzle without help. In order to find the swordmaster, you have to follow the old shopkeeper when he says he'll go talk to her for you. I thought that, and thus tried to follow him, but when I went to follow him out of the shop, he disappear with no indication of where he went. So I finally ask the game for a tip, and it says, wait for it, to follow the guy. So, I try again, and this time the game shows where he goes.
I keep following him until I enter the island map, right on his heels(literally), and guess what, there is no indication where on the map he goes. No sprite, nothing, so I ask help again, and it shows he went into the woods. This is not good design for a puzzle. It was likely not intended, but it's still a problem.
There are other cases of this, where the puzzles are either too vague to figure out, or fail due to the game not working corrctly, So this game is by no means perfect.
I would say this game is mixed, great narrative and characters, audio, and visuals, but held back by sloppy gameplay in some parts. I will give it a tip towards the positive end though because of the help button reaily available to help the player progress. If that wasn't there, I would not recommend this game due to some of it's overcomplicated and sometimes buggy puzzles.
Update: I finished the game, got bored of and frustrated with the puzzles 1/3 of the way through, and said screw it, I'll just use the "Help" botton through all of the puzzles just to minimize story progression downtime.
Good story, very entertaining, but the puzzles, to me, are so bad, I just basically skipped them. I thought this game needed some more love. The obvious highlight is being able to play as dinosaurs, and although the human gameplay is pretty standard-issue-FPS, being able to fight dinosaurs is pretty fun. This is even better when playing as a dinosaur, because you can go from stomping around as a Tyrannosaurus to weaving through the undergrowth and spitting venom as a Dilophosaurus to soaring around and dropping people off cliffs as a Pteranodon, all within the course of one match.
While the experience is fairly limited beyond multiplayer deathmatch, the developers are constantly adding and expanding to the game. Overall, I'd say it's the best dinosaur game around right now, right next to ARK.

I like it, it is way different then any controller I have ever used.

It's the world's most customizeable gamepad - There are a few games more suited to the basic layout of traditional controllers, but this controller is overall far more versatile than your average controller, and can get the job done that other controllers do as well (although just barely not as well).  Good for FPS games (single player), can even manage to play RTS games, and works just dandy for games like platformers and the etc.
The magic is really the software built into steam big picture that can map actions to your gamepad, rather than using the in-game bindings.  With macros and state-selection, a new method of mouse control and a handful of new trigger options -  These controllers can even manage to play MMOs.  Very impressed.
If you really like your Xbox controller, you probably won't grow too attached to the Steam Controller, but if you're more a keyboard + mouse guy, you might be pleasantly surprised with this controller / mouse compromise.

This game is simply amazing. It has something to offer for everyone; fast-paced and fun combat, great story, interesting characters, RPG elements, fun "minigames" (for lack of a better word), possible relationships with other characters (and especially Sky). The graphics don't look as amazing as they seemed several years ago, but the visual side is still pleasant to look at and very characteristic.
What made this game one of my favourites was the story. Even though it may seem a bit boring at the beginning, soon the story grips you and doesn't let go until you finish the game. Not only you visit interesting locations and meet various people (who actually seem like real characters and not just something generated for a game), you also make significant choices that affect the game's ending.
The last element I would like to mention is the combat. As for my character, I chose the Leaping Tiger style and after upgrading it to maximum, I think it's the best I could have chosen, maybe with an exception of Crimson Tears, but they require a lot of focus. But I loved the way you could learn new styles (Drunken Fist was hilarious) and that you could choose how your companion would support you (active/passive).
The only downside to this game is that the Steam version is somewhat buggy. In my case, the game was in slow motion. I managed to solve the issue, though I can't remember how. If you're unsure whether you would like this game, I recommend waiting for a Steam sale. If it's below 5 euro, you won't regret getting it.

DR3 is the generic Zombie story that you would expect it to be. The infection spread, you are a survivor and of course, immune to this plague. You play Nick, a mechanic genius that can combine pretty much anything together to create the ultimate weapon. The story is nothing new and the quests are repetitive. Most of the time, you will need to go fetch something for someone and that thing is always at the other side of the map. However, getting to the objective is the fun part of the game. This is where you will eradicate thousands of zombies in your way. There is a timer in the game to escape the city in like 6 days, but it's long enough to enjoy the story line, the side quests and maximum carnage. Completing chapters of the story will sometime fast forward the clock to fit with the plot but you will never feel in a rush to move forward until the last chapters. While you play the story, you will receive optional side quests to help survivors and you will be rewarded with experience, companions and/or weapons. With certain skills you will be able to have more than one companion at a time, and you can also equip them with basic weapons. Multiple collectables are scattered across the map that will give you exp and other perks. Also, when Nick levels up, he gains points to distribute in a good range of skills to adapt your playstyle. There is also multiplayer where you can play co-op and some other modes (I personally did not try multiplayer yet)
Now let's talk about zombies. There's a ton of zombies everywhere, and the fact that you can have a thousand zombies on screen is epic. Hacking and slashing through a sea of zombies is the most satisfying feeling you will ever have in a zombie game.  The world is open, with almost no loading involved (except for the initial loading, the loading if you die and some story moments (btw, loadings are kinda long)). As you progress in the story, more zombie types emerge that increase the challenge.  Of course, Nick knows how to build, and he builds good stuff. THe variety of weapons that can be found is great and the different blueprints available for combos and super-combos weapon is awesome. If you want to destroy a zombie with a flower pot, you can do it, but you can also do it with a motorcycle mixed with a Steamroller. There are a lot of choices at your disposition. No matter what you choose you will feel overpower and you will love it.
I recommend this game to any Deadrising Fans and zombie fans in general. I also recommend to have a very good PC to run it so you get the best experience. There's some fix that can be used to unlock the 30fps cap if you think your computer can handle it. Be aware that some people experience crashes and other problems with the game, so look at the game community for fixes or see if someone with a equivalent rig as yours have any issue.

Because those rarely work, and often ends up being to slow and so on.
That being said; this game is semi hardcore, and might turn out a little frustrating to some. I know a few Youtubers have "criticized" this game for being a dying simulator. Which in a sense is true, but only at the beginning when you treat this game like COD or BF. This is a arcade version of a war simulator. Something between Arma and Battlefield. Smoother controls and more practical solutions than Arma, but not so much as Battlefield, which makes this game feel immersive and realisitc. This game also allows for map editor, so the community if filled with custom made maps, tested and aproved by the Rising Storm community. How about that "any major game developer", who can't get anything right?
One of the best features in this game is the variety of characteristics of the different factions of the game. As a US soldier (same goes for the Aussi soldiers) you have better firepower and technology than the Vietnamese forces, but you lack mobility and agility, which allows the Vietnamese forces to get away quicker, hide and sneak around by using the underground tunnels and so fort. This creates a diverse and even matchmaking, allowing you to play out each match differently.
All in all a really good game. And with the constant updates we'll be seing new maps, items and factions often enough to keep us interested. And for less than 20 euros, you can't go wrong here. This is by far better than any other realisitc shooter out there. No pay to win, no restrictions, no "premium pass". Just good old fun.
And one thing this game has that no other game offers; the best looking air strikes and napalm strikes ever! They look like they're from a movie. And a epic movie that is!

While this game is tailored more to younger players, though that doesn't mean it's all bad. Yes, there are jokes only kids would laugh about, but there are definitely some genuinely funny moments as well.
The storyline is a bit more lighthearted than that of The Walking Dead games, too, but that's to be expected, since it's obviously a game about Minecraft. Again, this does in no way mean the story isn't compelling, since there are still interesting choices to be made and interesting characters to be met, but if you're someone who's looking for something dark and grim, this game might not be for you.
The five episodes this game consists of (so far) are roughly of average length from what I can tell; at least it doesn't feel like the storyline is rushed at any given point, which is good.
Typical TellTale game, only a bit more lighthearted, though  it still manages to have an intriguing storyline. I had my fun with it despite not being part of the "target audience", if you will.

tl;dr - Buy this for your 10 year old, don't expect much otherwise.
It does pull off the Minecraft aesthetic pretty well, but that's about the only good thing I have to say about this game.
The story and the dialogue is very much from a children's book - bad guy pops up, good guy (you, the awesome hero) save the day. That's not really a problem though, since I guess that kind of story is expected out of a Minecraft game since it's kind of marketed towards kids these days. What is a problem though is the way the story is set up. Now I'm going to spoiler it up because people get salty about these things or whatever, but it doesn't really anything from the story -
. Basically they sold an incomplete product as you would expect to get the full game experience WHEN YOU PAID THE FULL PRICE OF THE GAME. Also the story is very inconsistent. Like the guy you are supposed to hate suddenly becoming your best friend for no apparent reason inconsistent.
Other than that everything's as you would expect from a telltale game - essentially a FMV (movie) style game with QTEs thrown in where the story is effectively defined by your choices. Sadly in this one your choices don't really culminate much in anything, as no matter what you choose the outcome will be the same (with very minor differences that don't really matter at all). If previous Telltale games culminated with your choices playing a part in the ending, in this one the choices just kinda happens and no long matter 5-10 minutes after the choice's been made (I suppose sometimes some insignificant dialogue changes in the next episode or something).
And when playing do disable telltale's cloud saving. It has a tendency of losing save data and then syncing your old saves from before-previous session over your saves causing lost progress.

This game is... interesting. I purchased it upon recommendation from some friends. I was initially rather frustrated due to compatibility issues with modern machines - be warned, this game has some issues with Windows 8. If you are running W8, make sure you go into your SteamApps/common/Jade Empire folder, then run the "Jade Empire.exe" as an administrator - this usually fixes any issues you have with it. It also tends to be a bit disagreeable with dual monitors and alt-tabbing.
The game itself is typical of BioWare, before they really solidified their RPG formula. It is very reminiscent of KOTOR, minus a lot of the polish. The story is fairly predictable and cliché - it's almost to the point where I startred treating it as a martial arts parody. The big "twist" can also be seen a mile away, and it wasn't all that great either. Generic good vs. evil morality system, characters are fairly flat and one-dimensional. Difficulty is all out of whack and oscillates with little predictability, with some fights being frustrating, and the majority being too easy.
Overall, it's... okay. It's not great, but it isn't a bad game either. Definitely worth a try if you can pick it up on sale for cheap.

My PC: i7-6700 4.0 GHz, GTX1060 (6GB), 32GB RAM, Windows 10 64bit
OPTIMIZATION:
- The game runs at normal speed on my PC.
- I don't know if the framerate is capped at 30 but I get only 30 fps with Gentlemen of the Row mod installed. Dropping the settings to low doesn't help. And it feels stuttery.
THE SOMEWHAT GOOD:
- The map is big and there's a lot of activities.
- Story leans more toward realism than SR3-4.
THE NOT SO GOOD:
- Aiming, melee combat, vehicle handling feel wonky.
- Controls lag sometimes, e.g. getting in/out of the car, shaking the spray can, grabbing human shield.
- Button prompt doesn't show controller buttons. Installing Gentlemen of the Row helps. But if you remap the buttons, the button prompt doesn't change.
- SR2 forces you to do side activities to gain Respect and unclock next Story mission. So if you just want to do a quick run for the story, you can't. I think this interrupts the game flow.
- Despite the big map, different areas look the same. And the world feels empty.
All in all, this is a bad port, but not a bad game. If you get SR2 with the franchise pack (with SR3-4 and all DLCs, which are totally worth the sale price), try it and see if you like it.
I don't recommend getting SR2 separately though. People say it's the best SR, but I just don't see it.

Well, never thought I would (/could) say anything positive about this game.
This game had a rough start. Wrong intentions by the devs combined with the wrong type of playerbase.
This game should be, from the start, a PvP game. Team Death Match, Get To Chopper, Get to egg, gamemodes like that should be the modes with the most audience. But the playerbase that liked PC:E from the beginning (the Free Roam playerbase) wanted skins, and the devs really didn't mind that at all. They gave skins, tons of it.
The game didn't felt like the old PC, and thats all what we wanted. We, the actual PvP playerbase. I've tried this game several times during it's development, but never gave it me the same feeling as PC did. The game felt slow, a lot of things felt sluggish, overal it just wasn't good, not fun enough. That plus the fact that 90% of the servers were (/are?) Free Roam, and servers with actual PvP modes didn't had that much animo most of the times.
Well that beeing said, I thought today,  after the recent update, ''Lets give it a go, again..''. And I was very surprised, in the positive way. The pace is a lot higher, things felt much more smoother, the balance seems to be going into the right direction. Now there are still some flaws, it's not near perfect so to say. But, and that's a big kardashian but, the game is fun again. I actually enjoyed my time playing this game, like I did back in the day with PC. It seems like this game is finally going into the right direction, back to the real and true PvP aspect.
Unfortunately, the playerbase is still tiny. And still way too many Free Roam servers.
But if no one buys this game because of the lack of PvP playerbase and too many Free Roam servers, that will never change. This game feels actually good enough to play, and therefore it should be considered for buying if you are interested. It is worth your time, and money. All we need is more PvP players and bring back the epic battle's!

Interesting first design from Valve.
Put it simply, the Xbox One or Sony Dualshock 4 controller provide a better PC gaming experience when compared to the Steam Controller.
The biggest issue I had is the ergonomics of the handles. I have above-average hand size, and the controller felt large in my hands. The weight seems fine, but the grips just feel too big feeling uncomfortable in my hand.
The haptic touch pad is more annoying than useful, and the dual touches don't appear to offer a lot of functionality over a dual-stick.
The facebutton layout is a poor choice given that both Xbox and PSx controller layouts have the face buttons higher than the right thumbstick.
If you are a strong PC gamer, you likely have a favorite gaming controller. The Steam Controller isn't compelling enough to switch from that.
If you're new to PC gaming, skip this controller and go with an Xbox or Sony controller.

A profound, mature game based in the not-too-distant future where your actions and choices have consequences.
I couldn't be happier with how this game turned out. It remains very faithful to the original game in all of the areas that mattered. Best of all, it has completely overhauled the series' weak spots into some of its strongest features. The cover system makes stealth through the levels possible and even rather fun. The melee takedown system is nicely balanced and clears up the stragglers a satisfying, conclusive manner.
I've never liked the idea of robots or futuristic games, but this one gets it right. It grounds itself in reality by predicting where new and up-coming technologies will be in 15 years' time. It's evident that the developers have put a lot of thought into making this a grim but believable world. I get all smug every time I hear about augmentations on the news and how we're one step closer to the depressing orange world of Deus Ex. In a way, I want it to happen!
Deus Ex's main strangth has always been the choices it presents to you and how it faithfully follows your decisions to the end. You can kill as many or as few people as you like and the game will continue to carry on as if what you did was how it was meant to have been done. Brilliantly, failing an objective won't result in a 'game over' screen but will instead fill you with so much guilt that you'll be tempted to lose several hours' worth of gaming to try and do it right. For example- a couple might be executed by terrorists and you'll think nothing of it. The second time you play through the game, you may be able to save both and they're so thankful they invite you back to their apartment for tea and biscuits. The third time, one might die and you have to give the news to the other one, which is more heart-breaking than it should be.
There are still lots of pointless areas for you to explore should you want to. The levels themselves aren't as large as in the original game, but are still large enough to give you a decent amount of freedom. Occasionally the environment feels 'levelly' but for the most-part it feels like you have the freedom to do as you please. You can develop your character as the game progresses in basic but meaningful ways and it adds even more replayability to an already exciting game. Oh, and the music is brilliant and very memorable. I particularly like how you can hear songs from the original game on in-game radios.
The game itself is a little rough around the edges and I fear that it may age worse than other games, but for now it's the king of the Deus Ex genre. Now that the boss fights have the same degree of freedom as the rest of the game there is absolutely no reason not to give this game a go if you haven't already. I believe that this game has rebooted the series in the same way as Doctor Who has done in recent years and I'm willing to accept sacrifices and changes to the game if it means that today's generation can feel how I did when I played the original all those years ago. That being said, to say that this game is merely a shadow of the original would be an injustice. It's a step in a new and exciting direction and I can't wait to see what they do with the franchise next.

SVG 3 Step Reveiw (Story, Visuals, Gameplay)
A superb game all round, stealth is great, action is good and sandbox elements executed really well.
Story
The story is fantastic, the prologue pops you straight into the action and sets up what is to be a lengthy and immersive story on a great journey through numerous locations in a futuristic setting. I found myself fully immersed within an hour and loving the progression that is presented to the player for their experience, this made me want more and more throughout! Not once was i bored during this game, i found myself reading all the emails and notes through the game to build up the story and exploring every area so i found every one. 9/10
Visuals
Stunning visuals throughout, although they may not be to everyone's taste. The graphics are top notch for the generation and beautiful environments really add to the immersion mentioned above. One thing to note, which some may not like, is the yellow hue to everything, however, i feel this adds to the unique beauty of the game and gives it its stunning unique look (much like the green hue in fallout 3 for example). 9/10
Gameplay
Never a dull moment with the gameplay here, there are three approaches to every area:
> Stealth - sneaking around, ducking into vents, cloaking etc..
> Techno - Hacking, using robots and turrets against foes
> Combat - run and gun
Having these three approaches and being able to mix and match at any time allows for so many different combinations of dealing with situations that there is very little repetition. The one part that truly lets the game down here (and is quite infamous) is the boss battles, which throw this out the window and turn into a battle, however, this is disregarded as the directors cut overhauls this for the better! 9/10
Overall i loved this game, its rare to have such a good shooter in this day and age with all the rehashes and lack of innovation, this game is my personal GOTY.
+ Great Story
+ Stunning Visuals
+ Awesome sounds and ambience
+ Innovative gameplay
- Boss battles (fixed)
- Yellow hue may not be to everyones taste

I bought Jade Empire when I found it in a bin for exactly 2 euros. Years later I bought it again on steam for another 2 euros. All I can say is: money well spent.
A lot of people will tell you that Jade Empire is Bioware's weakest game. When you measure any rpg up to Knights of the Old Republic or the original Mass Effect, chances are your perspective is going to be a bit disadvantageous for Jade Empire. This isn't star wars, and this certainly isn't mass effect, but it is a unique game that has all the makings of greatness.
I was bummed out in Knights of the Old Republic when I learned that the combat would be dictated by a D&D dice roll system. This is the kind of uncertainty I hate, the kind of unrefined gameplay that has absolutely no excuse to exist in the modern world. Jade Empire does away with that and gives you live action, direct, fist to face combat. It has aged like a biscuit though. It is tough, rigid, and unrefined by todays standards, but a step up from the roulette style gameplay from Knights. Combat is fun for while, but you'll quickly find yourself looking for ways to dispatch your foes as fast as possible. The game offers various options. Martial Arts allow you to attack your enemies with your bare knuckles and are generally effective against all enemies. Elemental Styles allow you to throw fire or ice (bending if you will) at the cost of chi. Various weapons are very effective against humans, but useless against spirits. Support styles allow you to set up your enemies for a finishing blow. And at a hefty chi price there are the transformation styles that allow your to morph into a being of pure awesome to obliterate your foe. There is plenty of choice for you to customise your style, and the game gives you a fine world to flaunt your skills.
Jade Empire is set in an oriental world. Full of references to Chinese, Japanese, Indian and Bhuddist mythology. If you have ever watched Avatar: the Last Airbender then you should get the idea. There aren't many games out there like this and Bioware has done a great job at crafting a world that looks the part. This is the nice thing about Jade Empire. You'll want to walk around and talk to people, help them (or ruin them, you know the drill). In the end though you'll still be after the same thing thing: Saving your master. You play a martial arts student, whose life is uprooted when a secret orderer invades your hometown and kidnaps your master. Que the hero music and get to it.
It is a shame Jade Empire has ages so poorly. The controls are fluent as a beached whale, and the character models are not always as polished as they could be. Still, its universe and setting are unique and if you like a decent RPG of westen make then do not hesitate to get this.

How do I start...
Well, Minecraft Story Mode is a Telltale game, so if you've ever heard of other games of that type then you know what you're getting into.
If not, let me clue you in.
In Telltale games (at least, from the two that I've played), the big thing is that your dialogue choices cause different things to happen later in the game. Did you punch this guy? Well, later (episodes later) you can apologize when you realize his reasons. Did you come up with a secret handshake? Three episodes later it's time to use it.
There are also some walking around sections (quite a few, actually), and some quick time event sections (which for some reason don't upset me in these games, even though in 'normal' games quick time events annoy me. Maybe because it's actually a common game mechanic in these games? I dunno)
In this game, you control the main character of Jesse as they do many things such as:
Enter a building contest with their friends
Chase after their pig friend into the woods
Go to a back alley deal of a skull
Break someone's precious machine
Rummage through the guy from the deal's stuff cause he ripped you off
Save a friend who got stuck in a box when the other guy came back
Watch as a creature strong enough to destroy the world is made right in front of your eyes
Run away very, very, very fast
And that's just part of Episode 1.
I will say, when I heard about this game being announced, I actually avoided it for a while. I was worried it was just going to be a garbage cash-in on the Minecraft name, but this was also before I understood what kind of story they were going for and what a Telltale game was.
While yes, it is probably more aimed at a younger audience (because lots of kids play Minecraft), I actually really liked it. The story was interesting to me, I liked the characters (though being honest, I wish Axel had a different scream audio clip, and I wish Olivia's lines had a bit more emotion in them, but that's personal preference), and the gameplay was fun. The different dialogue options give a reason for replayability if you like the game in the first place, and the fact that we're getting at least three more episodes (and I hope there might be more after that, because I really do like these characters) would bring me back even if I wanted to stick with just one playthrough.

First things first: There's a lot of controversy surrounding this game being a bad port, having terrible performance and so on but I guess I was lucky since apart from some crashes at the beginning (which i solved by installing older nvidia drivers) I didn't experience any technical problems.
Second: I didn't play any of the older Dead Rising games just yet, so I can't really compare this new installment to those, but one thing's for sure, what Dead Rising 3 does, it does mostly well and I had a great time playing while playing it, although i'm a huge sucker for all open-world games.
The game looks great I never saw so many characters moving on the screen at the same time and fighting them is quite satisfying. There are tons of crazy weapons available through crafting for that and there's also an option for crafting different vehicles together and making something cooler. The gameplay itself is classic open world style, if you played Sleeping Dogs or any of the GTA games you'll know what to expect. Sadly the game also suffers from some of the issues that often plague these kind of games, for example the missions (especially the side ones) get quite repetitive after a while and although at first it's really satisfying to break through hordes of zombies with a vehicle by the end driving around the city gets really tedious. I think the length was appropriate for an open world game, if you want to finish all the sidequests and find most collectibles then the game (including all 4 DLCs) should last you more than 30 hours. There's a timer on the game (you have to finish it in 6 in-game days) which I found bothersome at first, but I pretty much did everything the main game had to offer in ~4 in-game days, so it's no real trouble.
All in all if you like open world games give this one a show, it's worth it.

Now that i have officially finished a pc port of this game, I can give an offical review of this game.
Story- The story for this game is one of the best in the entire series. I will not spoil anything major for those who have not played this game or saints row 1 on the xbox 360, which this game is a direct follow up to. Basically the character you plays as finds that his home of Stillwater has completely chaged at the time of his absence. Now he has to take down 3 rival gains to get his power pack. While this may sound like a "cliche" plotline, this game struck a perfect balance between both very dark and comedic emlements, and told the story in a very gripping way that activly engaged the player. Thewrefore the "cliches" are hard to notice. The game also has some excellent writing and voice acting that greatly ad to the immerson of the game's story. If you don't beleive me play it for yourself, then look up who voiced the main characters. Some of them will suprise you. Rating- 9/10
Graphics- the graphics may seem dated by the standards of the current generation, however i noticed very few texture issues or pop ins. It may not look like Doom 2016, but the game is still very apealling top look at. Rating- 7.5/10
Gameplay- The gameplay of Saints Row 2, as well as the other games in the series, is a 3rd person action-advenure game. As mentioned before, this game is set in the sandbox city of Stillwater. You complete various and unique missions in order to take down each of the 3 rival gangs. These can be performed in any order you choose, similar to the first game or the megaman games. In order to play the missions, the player must perform various activites or diversions to earn respect. i won't spoil the missions or actvities. Just take my word for it that this game has some very fun missions and awesome actvities. It also provides a decent challenge for both new and experiewnced players. Rating- 8/10
Soundtrack- The games soundtrack consists of licensed songs by real life bands and performers. While some of the songs may be hit or miss for some people, i personally thought thew selection of songs were very good and fit the tone of the game. Rating- 8/10
Performance and Add ons-  he Steam verson does have numerous issues; such as, fluctuating framerate even on a high end pc like mine, slightly stiff driving controlls, and, sometimes, crashes. The GOG version, on the other hand, has far less bugs and issues. While this game is not as smooth as the console version, it is till a decent port with just some minor and annoying issue. However, many of the games issues can be fixed by intalling the free "Gentelemen of the Row" mod. it is easy to install and not only fixe4s the game, it adds a wealth of new content to an already massive game. Personally, I do not think the mod helped the steam verson, but you can try it and let me know. I do think it greatly improved the GOG version however. Rating 6/10 (Steam) Rating- 8/10 (GOG)
Final Verdict- Buy this game. i cannot stress this enough. Despite the games issues, i belive it is a game anyone should play. It's that kind of game that has something for everyone.
Final Rating (Steam)- 7.7/10 Final Rating (GOG)- 8.1/10

At first glance, Out there Somewhere appears to be a simple Puzzle Platformer with a somewhat charming pixel aesthetic.
In reality... That's exactly what it is, though I don't feel that's actually too big a detractor, as while it is very simple, it does it all fairly well.
The game's layout reminds me of 'Switchblade' for the Amiga. A fairly linear platformer, though there are a good amount of instances in which you can branch out and find upgrades. There are a fair few, though they're never far enough from the main path to feel like backtracking to get the main game is a chore. How much they're all worth getting is questionable, as for all the cores, you don't get much more than an upgrade to make an already fairly easy final boss easier and the upgrade to the gun feeling like it only exists to make the boss right before the final boss completely pointless. The health upgrades feel like they're the only ones worth it.
The mechanics are solid and fun, and for the most part, the level design compliments it. The main gimmick of the game is the teleport gun, which is sort of like a one-shot portal gun. You shoot it, and you teleport to where the shot lands. The reason I use Portal as the comparison specifically is that the game mimics its 'Momentum is kept' idea, where if you're jumping when the shot hits, you'll be jumping when you get to where it was, along with falling, etc. It's fun and interesting, and aside from a few screens, it all blends together superbly. There will be a couple instances where the puzzles might feel a little too dickish, but if you sit down and think about all possible options, you should be able to get through, it's not horribly brain taxing.
The music is certainly a high point of the game though, and I can certainly see why they chose to make it DLC to get a little more cash out of those who want to support the developers a bit. For those who don't, they can just listen to it on Bandcamp (Although for those who want to /buy/ it on Bandcamp, it's 5 dollars, which is a little perplexing).
The story is definitely the game's weakest point though, and there's really not much more to it than what's described on the store page. No plot twists or anything. I won't spoil it for those who do want to experience it, since even an incredibly simple story such as this can be enjoyable to some, and the game does manage to give you more of a goal than just escaping the planet, but it's really nothing award-winning. That said, this game was made (According to the developers) to be a 'fun game based on what we used to play in the 90’s,' even following up by saying that It has a very simple story.
Also worth noting is the game's length. I don't believe in Steam's refund policy of a two hour time limit, as it kind of undermines a lot of fun games that are shorter than that. Most SHMUPs, some short story based games such as Grow Home (Haven't played the game myself, but has quite a following, and I hear the main story can be beaten in just shy of that time), hence why I'm not saying it's the weakest point for myself, though I know it can be for others. The game is fun enough to justify it in my eyes, but it only took 50 minutes for my first playthrough, and about thirty minutes for my second, which was an attempt at more of a speedrun.
I did get it on sale a long while back, only playing it now that I'm going through my backlog and I recall it going frequently on sale for about 50 cents, and for that, it's worth it. I'd still argue that's it's worth for two dollars. If the length throws you off, I'd recommend it on sale, and if it doesn't bother you, it's a whole-hearted recommendation otherwise. Far from perfect, but a fun time nonetheless.

This game is a mixed bag really, there's bits that work, bits that dont work so much. if you are a fan of the earlier games, this is prestty much the same deal gameplay wise, with the addition of vehicles that you can drive around and combine to make mad-max stle death machines. DR games have always been about zombie slaughter on a big scale and this one is no different in that respect, Kill zombies, get points, rank up to get get better ways to kill more zombies. there is a skill tree of sorts now, where you can spend point to customise your skills, though i am undecided if this improves the game or simply just isnt necesary. What the series is good at this game is also good at. In the normal mode, the story missions don't have the timer they had in previous games, and the survivors that you come across dont need to be escorted back to a safe house as before, so the tension that these two game devices brought to the earlier titles is missing, although i havent tried the nightmare mode yet.
In terms of performance, a lot of people have complained. But i think it depends on your standards. If you are expecting 60 fps minimum at max settings, you are not going to get that on anything. But i have a 5 year old pc and have tweaked the settings so the game is perfecly playable with hardly any dropped frames and at a higher detail level than the xbone.  If thats not good enough for you, you might be disapointed.
I would recommend this game for fans of the earlier games, probably not to anyone else.

Saints Row 2 is one of the greatest open-world adventure games ever made. Memorable characters, great gameplay, a large and detailed world, great story and writing, massive customization options, fun side activities – the total package remains stunning, even today. Let down by a sub-par PC port, though installing the community patch (the Gentlemen of the Row) and locking the framerate to 30fps fixed most issues for me. Worth trying at the list price of $10, and if you can get it to work, you’ll have one of the best bargains in gaming in your library.
Total size on my hard drive (includes Gentlemen of the Row patch): 12 GB
You can
.
Where to start with the good stuff?
+ Great story, sharp writing. Each of the gangs has a unique character that goes beyond the color of their cars and outfits. The Saints themselves are a fantastically individual group of psychopaths.
+ Great voice-acting.
+ Cool villains.
+ Simple, easy driving mechanics for a keyboard & mouse.
+ Stillwater is massive. Some open-world games contain obviously copy-and-pasted structures. Not here. Plenty of landmarks keep the areas identifiable and interesting.
+ Character customizer is very detailed. Want to adjust the look of your character in the middle of a playthrough (including a gender swap)? Visit a plastic surgeon. Tons of different clothes, accessories and tattoos are available as well.
+ Detailed auto customization. Whether your fancy is big rims or deeply tinted windows, gloss paint or matte, two tailpipes or four, there are a lot of modifications to make. Modified vehicles can be saved in your crib garage (all modifications save with it). Yes, even the Peterliner big-rig...
+ Customizable cribs. Choose décor and furniture.
+ Lots of things to do. Every activity that you see on your map? There are six levels of that activity, with character bonuses dropping at Levels 3 and 6 (like better accuracy, infinite weapon ammo, better health regen). And even after completing all of them (which will take a while!), there are other side activities that are started just by hijacking particular vehicles.
+ Lots of variety in the side activities. Fight in the ring, spray houses with sewage, set fire to everything on a 4-wheeler in a flame-suit, fake injuries for the insurance money, and many more.
+ Meaningful collectibles. Collect CDs scattered throughout Stillwater to unlock music tracks that can be added to custom playlists.
+ Great soundtrack. Whether your taste is Beethoven or Lloyd Banks, there’s something for you here.
+ The little stuff counts, and the little stuff is great. Whether it’s the funny radio broadcasts, homie banter, getting drunk, defending celebrities for cash or just flipping off random passers-by, it’s hard to get bored in Stillwater.
+/- If you haven’t played the first Saints Row game (which was never ported to PC), you’ll still have a good time. But there are a ton of references to the first game that are easily missed.
+/- Character animations are stiff. Saints Row 2 IS an old game, though.
+/- Shooting mechanics are average. They work, but they’re not special.
+/- Large number of weapons, though not all are available from shops. Some are only awarded after completing certain activities.
+/- Tons of driving. Stillwater’s size is awesome, but be prepared to spend a lot of time driving (or flying). And with amount of activities available, it’s easy to get side-tracked.
+/- As is, the graphics are decent, but not special. The FX Post Process Injector (originally made for Skyrim) works well for adding some visual flair (I like Preset 4). The Gentlemen of the Row mod also adds some additional graphics refinements.
- Horrible voice audio. The voice acting is good, but the sound is VERY compressed and raspy. (Music, cars, gunshots, and explosions all sound fine.)
- Lame boss fights. If you’ve completed any amount of side activities and acquired some bonuses, you’ll breeze through them.
- The side activities are fun, but be prepared for some Grade-A frustration when attempting the sixth (final) level of any activity. The difficulty ramps up to insane levels. Even with bonus health regen and a weapon with infinite ammo, completing a Level 6 activity relies as much on luck as skill.
- Awful plane and helicopter controls. One of the few places that Saints Row 3 is resoundingly better than Saints Row 2.
And now, a separate section just for the PC port issues:
+/- The Gentlemen of the Row community patch fixes many of these issues, but not all of them. There are also concerns about stability. The game has always run well for me.
- 60fps is possible – the game in general seems limited to 92fps, that’s what it hits in menus with v-sync off. In-game, it won’t hold 60fps, though. 45-52 fps is what I averaged. (Core i5 4590 + 2GB R7 260X). Adjusting the settings (including resolution) didn’t affect performance.
- At a frame-rate over 30, engine-driven cutscenes will have a variety of odd errors. Like a pistol the boss is waving around isn’t in her hand; it renders two or three feet to the side of her hand (the actual distance on screen is about an inch, but in the game world it’s more like 2-3 feet). Similar errors plague a cell phone in Akuji’s hand, the crash helmet on Tobias’ head… Lock the frame-rate to 30fps and the issues disappear (which is what GOG did when they released Saints Row 2 on their store).
- There is an issue with “speed up” where the game appears to be running at 2X speed. I’ve been lucky and haven’t had this issue, ever, but if you search the forums you’ll find a plethora of threads about it.
This review originally ended with something like, “Issues aside, Saints Row 2 is still one of the best open-world adventures out there. Go get it!” Unfortunately, the issues with the PC port can’t be put aside, making Saints Row 2 a buy-it-and-try-it purchase to see if it works. You’ll know if it does quickly (well inside the 2-hour refund limit). Hopefully, it will. Saints Row 2 is a slice of classic gaming that everyone who loves open-world adventures should own and play.

Jade empire is another great that time forgot. Lacking the major franchise tie-in of the Knights of the Old Republic series (or duo) and the triple-A investments of the Mass Effect series, this Bioware RPG is, imo, an underrated almost-masterpiece of a game.
As to the bad news: Getting this console port running on Steam and modern Windows machines ain't like dusting crops. A true PC gamer distinguishes himself from his console rivals by his literacy; he reads the forums (no, reads, READS the forums, you idiot, not reposts the same question that's been answered a million times, thus♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥off the veterans who could help if they thought you would/could actually read their response), finds the solution, and implements it, like a big boy. That's what you're going to have to do for Jade Empire, and it's probably a fair price.
The great thing about Jade Empire is the great thing about Knights of the Old Republic: You, the player, form your character. I'm not talking about a customization screen at the start of the game, or even stats and skills (Jade Empire actually falls short on these compared to Knights of the Old Republic, with its "streamlined" system), but the combination of the morality system with the diversity of fighting styles. There are weapon styles, martial arts, nuker magic arts, transformation styles(!), and a remarkable collection of creative "support" styles (things like mana draining strikes, various disorients, slows, DOTS, etc.). A large variety can be known, and you can transition between them on the fly, setting up the game's "harmonic combo" finishing moves or unleashing your own improvisational strategies. And Bioware didn't lay these arts out as a menu for you to wearily pick through; many of them are made available through questing or optional discoveries, or like the transformation styles, by defeating particular enemies. One of the best parts of the game, or any game, is an episode in the Emperial City, where you face down a foreigner by the name of Sir Roderick Von Fontlebottom, the Magnificent ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, voiced by John Cleese(!). After defeating him in a series of trials of wits and martial skill (if you can, the man's obviously your superior) one of the available rewards is Mirabelle, his muzzle-loading blunderbuss, as a weapon style. You can thenceforward barge through the game's normally-fluid martial arts combat, blasting first like a Harrison Ford character.
Mirabelle isn't a "necessary" skill to get you through late game; there's no such thing as a critical path of skill development. Which means you just take what's awesome. And there's lots and lots of awesome. There's the secret perk of the maxed-out double axes. There's the stunning power of White Demon martial style. There's the crazy OP speed of focus mode. There's the mighty disables of Storm Dragon. There's Red Minister transformation style, with crazy vampiric healing. You can get ALL of these, map whichever you want (up to 4 within easy reach) and then put upgrade points into your favorites without forgoing the others. Because styles provide benefits aside from raw damage, you're not confined late-game to your most upgraded techniques. They're your big guns, but even without upgrades you can still make practical and clever use of a wide variety of styles right up til the last fight. That's just good game design right there.
And then there's the writing. When Bioware's on, they're on. And this game is a top-shelf balance of drama and humor, one that is in my opinion, still unmatched. One of the major achievements is the integration of the morality system and your plot choices into your relationships with your many followers; that's about all I'll say about that. I'd just cheapen it with many words.

I'd rather confidenly say this is the best Fallout game in the series so far. All of them have great atmosphere and mood, but they also have their fair share of stupid mistakes or just plain lack of certain qualities. Fallout 2 eludes most of the failings of its predecessor and its successors and stands strong on its own as well.
It provides enough variety and character to feel full and alive, while staying true to the mood and maintaining the bar of quality at a reasonable level. Just as importantly, it maintains a very decent level of reactivity and non-linearity, and offers maybe not perfect but seriously flexible mechanics. It also introduces the best plot twist of the whole series. So all in all, I'd call it the purest and the most successful execution of the Fallout concept so far.
Even though I would love it to have more of the desperate and mysterious mood of the very beginning of Fallout 1, the vast pretty enviroments of Fallout 3 and the tasteful characterization of New Vegas.

I'm sorry to give a negative impression about this game, since it comes at only 1€, the minimum price here, and it's overall not that bad, but I wasn't able to enjoy it.
Graphics are retro-style, but badly rendered to me.. I don't know, I think this is a bad way to recreate '90s arcade games. Plus, there's no story and the game's quite short. Centered on three buttons, the most important being the teleport one; the other ones get you to shoot and to jump, nothing else. The teleport command will be of course fundamental in solving the small puzzles.
I'm feeling quite lonely 'cos it seems that everyone loved this XD
It's also easy apart from being short anyways, and it can take maybe two hours only, more if you're hunting for achievements like I'm doing.
Apart from the very first part, in which you're teleported into an arcade horizontal shoot 'em up, the rest of the game is a normal platformer as you have seen thousands of them. And the shoot 'em up short sectiosn are really really bad.
As I said, there's no plot at all.. the enemies crashed your airship and you've got to obtain your revenge.
All of these things summed up don't make a bad game, but to me as an adult gamer seem overall a copy of a copy of games I was already playing in the '90s, nothing really new is added and even if the price is low, you can play lots of free platformers way better and longer than this, with better soundtracks too.
It seems that when you are getting used to the mechanisms (which are as I said the same as many other older games) the game's already finished. There are no upgrades or other "new" things, and the store page mentions lots of masterpieces that really can't be compared to this one!
I also read of guys who finished the game in half an hour or something, and for 1€ it's not enough, especially considering the fact that there's no plot and there's also no replay value since it's the same and you can't do that much else.
For some reason this game should be extremely popular due to the hundreds of reviews it has. Anyways, to me it isn't worth 1€ for its value and its general content.
If you're into 2D retro arcade platformers, I'd suggest you to get this on sale 'cos at full price (and maybe it costs more in other currencies? I read reviews talking about 2$!) it isn't worth it at all.

The first time I played Saints Row 2 was almost 7 years ago. Despite the gap in time and the followup of several sequels, SR2 still stands tall as my favorite sandbox game of all time--and furthermore, probably the most fun one can ever have in a video game.
What's there not to love? The dramatic and serious story filled with rich characters and dialogue that still manages to be incredibly funny and surreal at the same time? The sheer amount of player agency loaded into every mission, every activity, and every objective? The power fantasy that must be earned by the skin of your teeth? Saints Row 2 has got it all, and more.
Stilwater, the ever expanding city of SR2, is filled to the brim with content and secrets. Unlike Grand Theft Auto and other Saints Row titles, there is an immeasurable amount of buildings and stuctures that can all be entered, such as the swath of stores, an underground shopping mall, a tourist cavern, a secret research and development lair, a recreational center, and a number of ownable and upgradable houses that the player may claim. From sports cars to jumbo jets to septic tank trucks capable of sprawing down the entire city block in feces, Saints Row 2 offers the player a number of vehicles to traverse the intricately designed urban sprawl, and does so with a big immature smile on its face.
The PC port is, unfortunately, subpar, but with the Gentlemen of the Row mod, most problems are easily brushed away and you are left with an incredibly rewarding and extremely fun experience that blows any other sandbox genre game out of the goddamn water.

Now, on to the specifics.
First of all, this isn't very much of a game. It's more like a Choose Your Own Adventure book in movie form. And actually, that ends up working really well. And despite this being a "kid's game", I assure you. Characters die. And you WILL cry.

I don't feel like getting into the "This Game is Stupid Because Minecraft is Stupid" debate, so I'll skip that one for now. But I do think the game, while benefiting from the Minecraft setting,  can stand on its own for people who don't like Minecraft.

Love this controller.  It is a mash up of exactly what I was waiting for since using half a controller and a mouse to play 3rd and 1st person games. Not being an usual controller fanboy, I wanted to get this one to see what the hype is all about and maybe play some games on it. I didn't expect it to work as well as it does, especially for its price.
Very customizable (even if just in big picture mode for now), haptics that don't actually suck, works with mouse&keyboard only games fairly well and you can type INCREDIBLY well with it, I'm actually surprised about that.
I however really dislike the triggers of it, they don't have nearly as much precision as I'm used to, and I'm not sure how much I'll end up using the touchpads over my beloved analog stick...
I'll recommend it because it works fairly well and does to some degree replace keyboard&mouse (even if precision of a mouse for FPS' isn't 100% there yet).

Software has dramatically improved since the early days, and I really love the controller for some games - much more precise than twin-stick.
Community templates are mixed, but often there's a very good one out there, so jumping into a game only takes a little trial-and-error.  BUT: if you hate configuring things, stay away.  You can customize this controller to truly amazing degrees, but you are forced to do this fairly often to get better than "pretty good" use with many games.
Unfortunately, touch detection seems... flaky.  Occasionally, seemingly at random, it'll think you moved your thumb half-way down the right pad for a frame or so of gameplay, then jump back to where you have your finger.  It happens often enough that it's uncomfortably jarring :|
To add to the downsides, it doesn't really "work" unless you launch a game _with the steam overlay_.  This crashes most games I'm interested in using the controller for, which is pretty unacceptable.  This is purely a software problem though, and the software has been improving a lot, so maybe it'll be fixed?
I'm debating waiting for v2, hoping they have slightly better hardware.  v1 is a mixed bag of mostly good, some excellent, and a couple almost-deal-breakers.

Well, I'm not a big fan of Hack & Slay games in general.
But this one added some elements that made it more interesting for me: Semi-automatic attacks instead of clicking marathons (btw bad for your health), strategic elements like several formations, character behaviour configuration, group separation and finally the ability to freeze the game any time to plan your moves and reorganize your party.
And there are easy to confiure hot keys on the fly to get e.g. just your melee fighters together for some special tactics.
But the balancing is a catastrophe. Dungeons are way too long where you can spend hours seeing the same enemies and building blocks again and again. And the AI behaves pretty stupid. They have a very limited field of view and you can easily wake them up one by one or in small groups even when you are surrounded by them in larger halls.
But if you accidentally get into a larger group that hits you a lot: Your health is regenerating very fast. So fast that using health potions is rarily required. And you can find tons of them. Speaking of which there is sooo many loot you can find that it's hard to manage all this stuff and have enough space to get the crap to the next town for sale. Don't let them lie around because they vanish after some time (especially if you change in-/outdoor environments).
At least you can have donkeys in your party that have plenty of storage for all your loot. But then you carry even more stuff around that needs to be organized.
Furthermore the story presentation is boring and you never have the feeling to care about people you meet. They are so dull. And quests are solved when you just did what you should do. That means you don't have to go back to report... it's like magic. This of course leads to a very linear experience. Also the levels are pretty linear. You can only move in restricted areas, you can't fall down and it's hard to die.
Verdict:
There are some good concepts in this game but it isn't executed very well so it gets boring after several hours of playing and finally its only annoying. But playing should be fun and never feel like plain repetitive work, isn't it? Because otherwise you should rather start to work on something useful.

As a long time Dead Rising fan this is both a heartbreaking game and a glorious return to form.
Yes, the fact that the game is capped at 30 FPS (though unlockable through hacks) is inexcusable in this day and age. The PC port is poorly optimized and is hard to run at acceptable resolutions and framerates and it's truly a shame...
Because when the game actually works, it's a ton of fun. While the game has lost some of the series identity it has gained in sheer madness and absolut craziness that can be achieved. The combo weapons are sometimes laugh out loud funny and the free roaming aspects are great. The absolutly staggering amounts of zombies are impressive as well and really gets your heart pumping when you have to traverse a giant horde. The city is massive, the story is as silly as ever and the overall feel of the game is great.
My biggest problem (apart from the port being bad) is that the main character is no where near as memorable as the other games protagonists (Frank West is my homeboy). This is somewhat fixable, from a purely cosmetic angle, with all the crazy outfits you can wear. That being said the character is whiny and unmemorable. Another issue is that the game is just too easy on its normal mode. I died once during my first playthrough and I didn't even use weapon lockers during my first one. It's very easy to become overpowered early on, making the game a cakewalk.
I would hold of for additional patches that fixes crashes and whatnot but I doubt they will get the game to run any better since the engine seems to be really poorly optimized. Its the absolute perfect pick up for cheap at a steam sale. If you can stand the shoddy port job it's a really fun game, with some truly hilarious moments and real madness. People have stopped by my computer and just stared at the screen going "What the hell are you playing?" all while I'm wearing a Groucho Marxx mask, a summer dress and slaying zombies with a giant teddy bear strapped with bombs and machine guns.
All in all, a really fun game but the port is appaling. Hold on until problems are fixed or if you can get the game for cheap.

From the wise hands of Ron Gilbert, Dave Grossman and Tim Schafer, along with the perfect ear of Michael Land, a rare pearl in the history of videogames has born.
Why is this game good? Simply because you'd replay it hundreds of times without being bored by the jokes, the landscapes, the puzzles, the extraordinary coordination between game depth and technical realization.
A simple story: "My name's Guybrush Threepwood, and i want to be a pirate". Nonetheless, a complex story, unique in its genre, which takes us to the discovery of unexplored islands, fancy characters (someone said Stan?), long-winded non-sense dialogues.
And then humor, humor, humor and humor again, the healthy one, the funny one, never inappropriate, that makes you laugh even if you don't want to.
Pros:
+ Double graphic engine: possibility to switch between 8-bit and modern version, very well crafted, caricatural and very coloured.
+ Excellent quality sound, with a very good dubbing track that brings justice to the good old muted version.
+ Humor, you're gonna laugh from the beginning to the end.
+ Classical point-and-click, simple and immediate controls.
+ Guybrush Threepwood
Cons:
- Replayability only if you're big fans of the series.
- Short if you really love point-and-click adventure games.
Final opinion: a must for a gamer, unforgettable for those who lived that period.

A modern version of The Sting! (Der Clou 2!) from 2001, where you perform different Heists and preparation missions in a variety of locations (Museum in Venice, several Banks, the Harbor, Police Headquarters, etc.) with 3 out of 6 different characters, all sporting unique skills.
The gameplay is an isometric real time stealth game, much like the Commandos series from 1998 - 2003, but here you can create a complete path for every character in pause mode and pause/play through the whole process. There are guards on patrol, cameras to disable and items can be picked up and used, which are basically 1 time uses of the different sills from the characters.
You gradually unlock characters, one of their 4 skills, tools and items in the story missions and there is a challenge mode for people that need more.
The story is about a Heist gang in the '60 being betrayed by one of their own and taking revenge a few years later. The characters are cliches, but all fits together to give you the " Ocean's 11 in the '60"  feeling.

Recommended.
This game is a real-time tactical heist simulation with the option to pause. You will have a variety of "crookz" to choose from to make up your team for each heist, and eventually you'll get the option to choose the order in wich certain heists are done. Taking you from heist to heist is a storyline that sets back in the 60's, but from how it plays out it's more like this game tries to capture the air of the 60's TV-shows rather than of the 60's itself.
The different maps have an objective to be solved, either place something, take something or similar, and there's several ways to solve a map. There's different types of obstacles to overcome and so what it comes down to is mainly sequencing. Each map also give you an introduction about the objective and give some suggestions about possible approaches. From time to time these introductions become somewhat long in my opinion, but they can be skipped, as can story cut scenes.
Overall, for anyone interested in tactical games, this game is a good option, and if break-ins, heists and the likes is intriguing for you, this is a very nice choice.

Ah Aura Kingdom, the game where I was thinking that I'd have fun, but in the end...there were a lot of things missing.
Pros:
So let me talk about the good news. Aura Kingdom is, in concept, a bit of a good game, the graphics are decent, the gameplay is nice, flashy, and fast. They can even be used to maneuver out of enemy attacks. Whereas enemies have attacks that can go everywhere. Before hand, multiple bullets similar to the manner of Touhou were shot from bosses, but it appears it's been nerfed, possibly.
The character customization is furthered, but not particularly with attire unless you're loaded. But it's still a bit diverse, although missing body style and form, every female charater is the same height as any other. And the same for males. There's only one race, Human, though part of the customization can end up making you look like a cat. Although that's just one of the options.
Cons;
Despite the flashy gameplay, skills can have a low cooldown, and you have no mana. So you can keep spamming the same rinse-and-repeat over and over. Basically making the game linear and predictable. Now occasionally, there are some quests where you play as something else, but that's only for during that quest, and most of those quests aren't even repeatable.
The plot itself, despite the basis of what you are (An Envoy of Gaia, blessed by some power or whatever), the game explicitly states that it's just a gift, and whoever gives it doesn't limit whether the power they wield is used for good or evil.  You have no choice of being good or evil, just good. Which having an evil storyline going against the protagonists of the story would prove useful. And a not so predictable choice.
The main quest is usually linear as the plot itself. Except you're a soldier in your hometown's garrison. During a turn of events, it turns out you're blessed by Gaia, but you're sent away by the Captain because the main antagonist of the prologue was also an Envoy. You then go on a quest to get rid of your Eidolon, a familiar that practically proves you as an Envoy, but because of everyone elses' ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. They're too preoccupied or too much of a xenophobic jerk to listen to what you need. And ironically enough, just about every player is also going through this. And the NPCs would act like as if you're the only person to ask for the sake of making you look like a protagonist.
Fast forward about thirty more levels throughout all of the stuff that's happening, and the device that's supposed to separate you from your Eidolon ends up not workng because of the ♥♥♥♥in' fact that you've bonded with said Eidolon, even if you've never even used it during the story. As a result, practically most of the story ends up being pointless out of the result of '♥♥♥♥ you and the time you spent doing this useless story'. You're given a purpose after all of that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. Where you end up serving the Templar's army. You eventually come across the big bad around this time, but mainly only in visions and chasing him all over the place as you race against the clock to build up the army.
When you hit LV 55 there is no story to continue to do, just another quest that tells you to go to LV 60 without any other quests safe for dailies to boost the EXP that you gain. As a result, you waste even more of your time, whereas fully raiding the Solo modes, at even on a CHALLENGE difficulty (where honestly by this time you're decked out with great gear, barely dying unless you're careless to an area-of-effect attack that's constant.) But even then..All you really get, even with a 40% EXP boost if you're fortunate enough. You'll get about a level or two and about 20%.
The Economy's a travesty, mainly from lack of appraisers, aside to greed of players getting too hopeful that some rare item they got is definitely worth a thousand gold, which even with dungeon raiding and selling everything you get, even near the initial endgame level (60), you'll be lucky if you 'earn' that much unless you go ahead and sell things on the auction house, waiting for some chump to buy it from you. Unless you list it at a reasonable price, like 5 gold. Aside to having the luck to getting such strong items. Or making them, but usually making them costs pretty much more time and even then, ridiculous amounts of gold compared to how much you earn dungeoneering. Whereas questing would be the only way to get a decent amount.
So in hindsight? Would I recommend this game? Probably not. If you wanna go for it? Give it a try.
