Edit2: This review is currently outdated, the last update was about 2 weeks since release date. Many patches and hotfixes have been sent out then and I expect most of these issues have been resolved. When time permits, I'll update this and give it a proper review.
I'd like to be more descriptive about the problems than my other fellow negative-review players. This game is riddled with bugs and crashes. I know you should expect nothing to be flawless on the first days, but this is far from acceptable and barely margins on playable at points.
To start the system requirements and the optimization of this game are terrible. I've played many games far and wide set to max with rarely anything dipping below 30 FPS and soaring easily otherwise. But setting this game on even the preset of "Medium" leads to severe FPS loss during any sort of strain. Mostly from either 100+ zombies or any cutscene I've experienced so far. Playing on low has allowed me to play with frame rate drops mostly on extreme cases such as ~300 zombies or to watch cutscenes without desyncing/skipping.
Come the evening of 9/10, the first patch was made including a fix to native resolutions. I can play now at 1440x900 and see the entire UI and gamescreen normally.
And of course, all the crashes. Almost all of them completely unprompted. There's not something that triggers like too many zombies, or a certain scene, it's just all seemingly random. Swing your sledgehammer? That's a crash. Saved a survivor? That's another crash. Threw one too many tires at Rhonda because the campaign won't progress on Chapter 0? Another crash. So many crashes, half your campaign will be navigating Steam to save any last shred of patience you have with this game.
So it all boils down to being issues around graphic quality and crashes. Everything else is fine, and believe me, I had fun while it lasted. But I've bought two copies because there's no local co-op. I have to battle through the finicky matchmaking system to play with my wife. And then, only to have it turn out to be a Disneyland Tour of the Walking Dead for my wife because the connection is so poor and hard to maintain. Even the cutscenes desync, lag severely, and randomly speed forward. You'd figure the one thing that is a constant with all clients aside from costumes would work normally. All to end with her crashing 20 minutes later. It's a disappointment.
It's a good, fun game. But it will be tarnished by all these flaws until patches or hotfixes go into effect. If you're a Dead Rising fan, tell the developers to fix these problems. There's a nice forum board where thousands (not exaggerated) of bug/crash reports have been made. And all that's been addressed by the development, or at least the forum management, is that they've redirected consumers to the community's fixes to these problems. And yeah, that's right, the community is currently more active about giving fixes on day one than the developers ever gave this current date.
TL;DR.
It's a poor port, seems very little work went into making it for PC. Matchmaking is indirect. There are several unprompted crashes.
Patch on 9/10 fixed resolution issues.
Other problems yet to be fixed, but seems like progress is at least being made.
I'll be glad to update this as a positive if these problems are addressed.
Good luck, and hopefully all of us who bought it will enjoy seamless gameplay one day.
Edit: Added more details. Also proofreading. First patch was made, resolution problem has been resolved. (Will keep an eye on future updates and update this review as necessary)

I was expecting it to be a lighthearted game where cats turn into people and all you do is flirt to get their attention while drowning in catnip and inneundo. The story turned out to be more complex as you find out more about the cat curse. However, your options to deal with the curse are limited. Your focus remains on interacting with the other characters to decide whose route to land on. Each character is well-written and I loved each of their personalities. They felt realistic, and I would I love to know them in real life. I wish there would be a sequel or extra side stories.
There are a total of 6 routes, including the secret Graves route (unlocked after you complete all the other routes). There are several common scenes with very slight variations. Fortunately, there is a fast forward button to speed through them if you want. There is only 1 ending per character, and 2 common bad endings. On average, it took me 1.5 to 2 hours per route.
The story was original enough to get my attention. It has its cute moments and is peppered with humour. However, it could have used more depth. Only one route (
) explored the difficulties they face from the curse e.g.
Ok, so maybe this isn't a priority since it's really all about Avery, but it would have made the story better.
I thought everything would be explained in Graves's route (common for secret routes), but his ending was rather abrupt. I was disappointed that they didn't fully explain about his past
, and about how this whole situation happened. I think a DLC prequel or sidestory would help close the loop.
There is no voice-acting, which is fine because the dialogue and characters' expressions manage to capture the tone. The opening theme song doesn't appeal to me but the rest of the music is on point. DEFINITELY not your typical third-person shooter. It's some game which can get intense, but can't be taken seriously. I mean.. LOOK AT HELGA! So anyway, the free-to-play concept is amazing.(Take notes, everyone) The standard currency are Blutes, which are used to upgrade your weapons, blah blah blah. The premium currency, on the other hand, is used to buy customization items. Basically, you need to play the game to get better, but you'll need coins to be fancy while doing it. The prices are pretty fair and it doesn't milk money out of you like others. (Looking at you, EA and Activision) But then again, that booty's all you need. OKAY getting out of topic here. So to get Blutes, you just need to play a full game. They give you small bonuses for performance, victory and stuff, but they're really small. Even if you're bad at the game, you'll still get a decent amount of em and everyone wins. The customization has a gigantic variety. You can create countless combinations of weapons which all have their ups and downs. From rifles to rockets, pulses to beams, these bad boys are deadly as no internet connection. Now the gameplay is a hella fun. It'll slowly suck your soul. I've played for about 30 hours the last two weeks, and I'll say that it has been a great 30 hours. Anyway, anyway, there are 2 game types so far. Casual and Ranked. You unlock Ranked at level 10 and Casual is available from the start. There are a lot of gamemodes. For Casual, there are Extraction, Death Snatch, Blitz, Jackhammer, and Domination. Extraction, being my least favorite, is a mode where you bring some kinda chemical, Blutonium, to a machine. Death Snatch is pretty much Kill Confirmed, where you kill someone and take their Blutonium to gain points. Next up, Blitz. I think it's like Control Point, where you stay on a certain point to capture it and gain points. Now Jackhammer is my favorite gamemode. It's like Capture the Flag, but with a twist. You can use the "flag" as a weapon which is a one-hit wonder. And I have yet to try Domination. I haven't reached level 10 yet so I can't really explain the Ranked gamemodes. So if you've reached this point of my review, I salute you. This is my poorly formatted review.  Being an indie game, this really shows the potential of what they can do. This is an amazing game which in my opinion, impacts the development of games and hopefully teach game companies a thing or two about these kinda games. Overall, I give this game a whopping 10/10. My favorite game so far. Play it. Love it. Throw your life away.

Bloodsports.TV is a moba type game where the main goal is to survive with your team mates but will you want to play it ?
Bloodsports. TV has a very simple concept. It play's like a online battle arena, but the goal is not to destroy the base of other players. This game is a wave based survival game where the main goal is to protect a rocket and fight until the game is over.

I didn't encounter any bugs while playing the game. There is a minor problem where sometimes my character wouldn't do a spell even though I had enough mana.
Overall Bloodsports.TV is a really good idea and the execution is really good, but the game is dead and playing Solo isn't that fun.  I do suggest trying the game if you have friends who play it or you don't mind playing solo. I give Bloodsports.TV a 7/10

I went into this expecting another run of the mill MOBA and, while that wasn’t far off, there was a bit of a twist on the genre. Bloodsports.TV is a multiplayer online battle arena game from Fatshark and Toadman Interactive. Let’s get rocking.
The Good
By now you’ve all played either League of Legends, or DOTA, or Smite, etc. Or, you live under a rock. My first experience in the MOBA world was Guardians of Middle-Earth and I anticipated every other MOBA I played after that would be, essentially, very similar. While B.TV is similar to your run of the mill MOBA, the object of the game is different and a lot less stressful. Rather than fighting the enemy team, you’re working with your team to defend your base against waves of enemies. It’s a blast.
I love the artwork in this game. I’ve been a fan of it ever since i first played Krater, another great addition to the gaming world from Fatshark. It’s like a less serious, Fallout style post-apocalyptic wasteland full of Scandinavians. What’s not to love? And the character designs are just fantastic.
The music is great, the controls are simple, the items are creative and fun, and the horde-style gameplay will keep you coming back for more.
The Bad
There wasn’t really anything that turned me off to the game while I was playing. We can just move along.
The Meh
Because it’s not one of the bigger name MOBAs, the community is pretty small and all but dead as far as I can tell. Don’t let that deter you though if you’re really wanting to play. It’s a fun game nonetheless.
Also, you have to pay to get the game itself, unlike other MOBAs.
Verdict: Yea
Bloodsports.TV is a solid MOBA game and, if you’re a fan of Krater, you’re going to like it. If it goes on sale, don’t hesitate to pick it up and give it a try. As always, thanks for reading.

This game was fantastic back in its day.  It's a contemporary of the original Neverwinter Nights, and while that was more for the cerebral D&D style RPG gamer, Dungeon Seige married hack and slash with RPG in a new way.   Rather than be like Diablo, it went the direction of being linear, giving a bit of an epic-tale sort of feel.
Unfortunately, I can't recommend it for purchase and use on newer machines.  It's not natively Win7+ compatible, which is normally not really a problem, but its older code for graphics management bleeds over to cause some pretty nasty glitching in HUD graphics and gameplay stuttering on nicer machines.   I'll need to run it in a virtual machine, which is beyond where most gamers are willing to take something they pick up on sale.   It may also run a bit better on ARM processors or similar systems that do not have discrete video cards.
As a game, 8 of 10.   But only buy it if you have something crappy to run it on; otherwise, you'll look to the sequels.

One of my absolute favorite old school isometric PC RPGs, and it's also one of the first games I played on my first real gaming PC. I somehow actually stilll have the intact box and CDs sitting around in storage somewhere.
You control up to eight characters at once, including a pack mule to act as extra inventory space. Characters can be specialized in a few ways, with two different schools of magic, ranged, or melee attacks. If you are feeling saucy, you can combine and make a hybrid class, such as a spellsword or some kind of other variant. You can succeed with nearly any party combination, so there isn't much pressure to min/mix the perfect party combination.
Combat is very micro-heavy, with lots of little subtle things needed to keep your party fighting in top shape. Although the game starts slow, you'll very quickly end up with a party of four to six characters and you'll be slashing through huge parties of monsters. You'll need to pay attention to what spells are being cast, positioning of your characters, and more; it's very consuming and very satisfying when you get through an encounter unscathed.
With a modern eye, though, there are a lot of rough parts to the game. Camera control is a pain, and controlling your party can get really overwhelming when you have a ton of characters. With casters, it can be clunky to switch between spells in combat. I really enjoyed this game and I still enjoy it to this day, but it might be hard to get for someone who didn't play it back in the day.

If my controller ringing, this was a triumph, Every time it turned on Wasn't awesome enough, The slew of other Versatile features will Hook you quick. If you hate tinkering and adapting, this is probably not for you, but what that means is that you have to accept always switching between something like an Xbox controller and the keyboard and mouse. The tradeoff here is that you can play absolutely any game from the couch, desk or while standing.
That's not to say there won't be a steep learning curve, however, But once you get The hang of the track pads and the customization options, you'll find yourself loving the feeling of jumping into any game, Whether originally for the keyboard or the controller, with ease. Steam saves all of your unique or community controller configurations for every game automatically and loads Them up again when you launch in the future. Rather than stick with what the developer wants you to, you can essentially have the same controller Scheme across all games. I found community configurations for almost all of my games and They are a single click away. Even for games like dead space 1, that have no built-in community configuration, after I played a few of the community of configurations with other games, it's easy to build my own in only a few minutes. Once i perfect my dead space 1 controller mode, I can upload that To the Steam Community for all of us to enjoy.
On the complaint Side though, It's strange that you can't do the exact same things by Plugging in a 360 controller, for example. Third-party controllers seem to only allow button customization once, in a universal fashion. Keep in mind I'm using the launch edition or version 1.0 steam controller And This will obviously change, but after an entire month has gone by, Steam still hasn't fixed a very annoying issue not allowing me to use both steam controllers and my third party Xbox controllers simultaneously. Compare to my 360 controllers, the steam controller really hurts my thumbs and hands after many hours of play. I get actual blisters on my Thumbs from simple games like Super Meat Boy. This is a combination of the pressure I must use on the shoulder buttons, the small size of the face buttons and the angle at which my Thumb hits the analog stick. You get over it after a few days, but expect actual real world pain from playing video games for the first time in years.
The battery life of the controller using just standard double A batteries makes me think of the original Xbox console hard drive. back in the day, that systems storage Seemed to never empty. In the same way, the steam controller battery indicator seems to never drop even after many hours of play. I'm still using the Same batteries since I opened the controller last month. Imagine how long it'll last with energizer Ultimate Lithium batteries!
My biggest surprise about the steam control Is how much I love using it as an HTPC controller. My keyboard broke and so I've been using the Steam controller exclusively to handle everything on my computer. In fact, I'm writing this review using nothing but my Steam controller and voice typing on Google Docs.
Finally, I'd recommend the steam controller to most PC gamers because valve has been updating steam and the steam controller firmware between every day and every week since its launch. They clearly care a lot about Its growth and the community and I can't wait to see what they have in store in terms of features in the coming months.

This game is fantastic, but I can't quite say why in a regular review, so let's take this by category.
The main attraction of this game is the teleport gun. This gun acts as a normal projectile when fired, but it doesn't hurt enemies. Instead, it passes through them until it hits a wall. When this happens, your character is teleported to the location that the projectile hit!
Later in the game, you find a regular gun, which acts just as you'd expect, hitting and destroying enemies.
There are also tractor beams in the game, which, depending on their color, will either change the trajectory of your teleport bullets, destroy your teleport bullets, or act as regular walls, activating your teleport bullets.
I give the mechanics an 8/10. They are very unique to this game, and are very fun to use!
There aren't many items in the game. You start off with the teleport gun, then later find the regular gun. There are collectible alien artifacts and abandoned cores that increase your max health and upgrade your
, but they're far from required.
I give the items a 6/10. There isn't much variety, but what's there is nice.
The controls are similar to that of an online flash game; The arrow keys move your character, Z jumps, X shoots your teleport gun, and C shoots your regular gun once you get it. It's easy to get used to, and feels natural. The platforming is sharp and percise, unlike other games like this that use bad platforming mechanics as a difficulty aspect.
I give the controls a 10/10!
This game is fairly easy overall, though it has some parts that I feel are unnecessarily difficult. Some of the mechanics are hard to learn, but once you do learn them, they're easy to repeat.
I give the difficulty a 7/10. The balancing could use some work.
Overall, I give the gameplay an 8/10.
Story is almost nonexistent in this game, but I kind of like that. The story can be summed up in just one sentence: "You're the good guy, and the bad guy ran away, so you have to catch him." The characters, however, are pretty bland. Only a few of them have any personality, those being the player character, the villain, and the entire species of tree... guys.
I give the story a 5/10.
[/b] MUSIC [/b]
The music. Good God, the music. I would buy the soundtrack to this game twice if I could! (I mean, I CAN, but I won't because money is a limited thing.) The music perfectly matches the theme of the game and every song is perfect for the area it's played in. Every song is nice to listen to, and I sometimes find myself turning on the sountrack for no reason.
I would give the music a 20/10, but I'm stuck with 10/10.
The makers of this game did a great job with the visuals of this game. Everything from the backgrounds to the animations to the finer details of the pixel art looks amazing and is easy to look at. This is one of the few games I can play without my eyes hurting.
I give the visuals a 9/10.
Overall, I give the setting an 8/10.
This is an easy category for me because there are no bugs! At least, none that I've found.
I give the bugs a 10/10! The developers made this game air-tight!
This game runs at a consistent FPS, and never crashes. Although, I have a PC made to run games like Skyrim and Chivalry, so this probably isn't a fair category.
The performance gets a 10/10 from me!
There were a few other categories I used for the technical stuff section, but they were too short to include.
Overall, I give the technical stuff a perfect
10/10!

In this game, you play as ScaryGirl, an orphan who was adopted by an octopus. You use one of your arms, which has become much like an octopus tentacle to whip, swing and climb your way through the 21 different levels. All the while trying to stay alive, collect gems, and pull up blackweed in an effort to get "Perfection" on the levels. By collecting gems you can purchase attachments for your tentacle that allow you to accomplish different things: hit harder but slower, hit lighter but faster, attract items to you, fly further, swim faster, as well as buying combos for added attacks. You can also purchase collectible "vinyls" of the monsters encountered in the game. I don't see any purpose in this other than obtaining the achievement where you buy everything in the store.
This is a standard 2D platformer with some isometric views. For the most part the controls are solid. It is when the view changes perspective that the controls go a little wonky. When this happens during a jumping sequence then it is death. There goes "Perfection." My time is clocked on Steam at 10 hours. At least 2 of those were trying to get past this exceedingly difficult area when you are on an airship and there are mob after mob of guards - they block your hits. There is only one checkpoint and no fish to eat and restore health.
Combat is satisfying. You can hit hard or light. With hard hits you throw enemies into the air and can juggle them for extra points. When enemies are near death you can grab them to do other things: throw them into other enemies, smash them into other enemies or use a special ability to squeeze them for health, turn them into a tornado or use them as a pogo to bounce away or to a high ledge. The enemies are varied and different attacks work better on different types. There are three or four boss fights, excluding the last boss fight. Each of these are good and varied. All require manipulation of the environment in order to win.
All-in-all this is a good platform game, but doesn't offer anything unique. The camera and controls feel right except for a couple of areas and this means death. There are a couple of places that are extremely difficult including the aforementioned airship level. In the end, it is worth playing if you like platform games and you can get it on sale. It is fun, but I don't see myself replaying or attempting to get "Perfection" on all the levels.
Interesting premise, but poor optimization and a rushed production leave this one feeling rather anemic.  Recommended for those who really like platformers, but not really anyone else.

If you happen to have played Irisu Syndrome by the same developer, this one can be described as Irisu meets Touhou, without any scary surprises.
Otherwise, to explain it simply, it's a vertical bullet hell shooting game with an empashis on bullet canceling. You can shoot only one bullet at a time, and while it does clear enemy fire as well as damage them, relying only on that is going to get you killed fast. Instead, you can shoot the colored shapes that appear throughout the level at a steady pace and try to make them bounce against each other: the block will soon explode and destroy anything in its area of effect. Each time the block you shot bumps into another one of the same shape and color, it will cause the second one to explode too, as well as increasing the power and radius of the blast.
That means that rather than squeezing through minuscule openings, you're encouraged to make use of the puzzle-like system to find the perfect moment and angle to hit the blocks and stop the bullets before they even reach you at all. This easy to understand core mechanic remains unchanged for the whole game, but never gets boring as you start to master it and find new ways to save yourself from a difficult spot. The two characters play similarly, with their normal shot being the biggest change: Kairi shoots a bullet that travels to the end of the screen and back, while Satsuki has a short range shot with much higer knockback and creates bigger explosions.
Another important difference from other shmups is that this one doesn't have extra lives or power-ups. Instead, you have a health bar, that can be occasionally replenished by picking up health items, and there is
at all, so you can't just let yourself hit it to pass a pattern. You do however have the traditional smart bombs for emergency situations.
Bosses work like Touhou, with the added bonus that some of their attacks are optional and come in the forms of "duels": if you play well enough, the boss coughs up a little red blob, and picking it up initiates an additional pattern. These create
great opportunities for high-scorers, while beginners can easily ignore them with no repercussion.
The game has 5 main stages, which do get progressively more challenging but are easier than what you'd find in most "pure" STGs, and an extra 6th stage which ramps the difficulty up to eleven. If you're going for completion, be ready to have your patience tested. There is also a survival mode where you can try to endure the enemy assault for as long as you can, and a absurdly difficult "hard mode", that is thankfull not required for anything.
Beating the game should take from 2 to 6 hours depending on your skill level and dedication, while clearing it 100% will extend the longevity quite a bit (took me more than 20 hours to manage everything, just to give you an idea, although to be fair I'm not a master player).
Interestingly, despite being a shoot-em-up, a visible amount of care went into the backstory, which you can unlock little by little by collecting the achievements. It's not the main focus of the game, but it's nice to have a sembiance of plot that is not just a complete excuse to shoot things down, and it's a nice rewards for those willing to go the extra mile.
As for the technical side: enemy mobs are pretty much all variations of the same design, sadly, but the character and bosses' portraits are much more detailed and good-looking. The soundtrack is also easy on the ears and goes perfectly with the flow of the game, especially during the later levels.
I didn't encounter any notable bug, and can confirm PS3 and PS4 controllers both work fine.
:
+ Unique gameplay concept
+ Interesting lore and backstory
+ Good OST
+/-  Challenging.
-  Slightly lazy mobs design and behaviour. Visual effects could also be a bit better.
-  Relatively short if you don't care about completion.
A breath of fresh air in the genre, and a completely unique shoot 'em up that any fan of the genre should be able to enjoy.

Unexpectedly good and ridiculously underrated, but not without flaws.
This is a game about clearing bullets off of the screen - this shouldn't be compared to Touhou or any of Cave's shmups, simply because you have a lot more control over the bullet density. The mechanic for clearing bullets off of the screen is simple - you shoot one of the colored blocks and it explodes, clearing bullets. If the colored block hits a similarly colored block, then the explosion is larger, in proportion to how many blocks you hit.
Usually, there's two different colors. The fact that you can choose which colored block to hit opens up a lot of very good mixed strategies for the veteran, which makes the game mechanic significantly more fun than it would be with just one color. There's harder stages with three colors, which has the effect of making things easier if you are very good, and harder if you are not.
The artistic style is incredibly good. First, the bullet patterns are fresh. Most bullet patterns in most games have the effect of pushing the cautious player down, but the cautious player in this game will sometimes feel himself pushed upwards, which is interesting. You really feel like you're using the entire screen to play very often, which is really good. Second, the art itself, though unpolished a little, is quite beautiful. Last, however, the music is absurdly good - "bringing you to tears and making you serously consider buying the OST" good. Perhaps the first thing I thought with respect to the style was that this is the game most US indie gamers wish they could make - a game that is undeniably a piece of art, but without any of the pretentiousness that typically burdens such games.
I must admit that I take issue with three things: first, the second stage is notably harder than most of the rest of the game. This feels incredibly unbalanced. For someone who is good, this will not matter much, but it is not a good thing. I can imagine this being a significant hurdle for someone new. I would have put that particular opening sequence in a later stage, but the burstiness of it definitely fits the character of the second boss.
Second (spoiler), there does not appear to be indication in-game that you should not destroy the last stage midbosses in order to get the good ending. This is very counterintutive.
Third, there is not a middle difficulty. The unprotected mode feels like "Hard" or "Extra Hard" mode, while the protected mode feels like "Easy" mode.
The third flaw makes me hesitant to categorically recommend this game - I thus conditionally recommend it. If you're starting out and trying to branch out, the protected mode of this game is a good way to do this. If you're mildly skilled (using Touhou as a yardstick, 1cc'ing most Touhou games on normal being no challenge, but 1cc'ing most Touhou games on hard being a bit beyond you) and you want a sort of challenge, the unprotected mode of this game is definitely a way to go. If you're very skilled, then perhaps spending 8 or so hours admiring the art and bullet patterns is worthwhile.
The only group of people I must say who should avoid this game are people who have a low, but not very low, level of skill. Unprotected mode will be too hard, and protected mode will be too easy.
Get good, then blow $5 on this game. The experience will be very worth it.

Ingenious game that combines a shooting game with puzzle elements. At first it may seem the puzzle element overshadows the shooting game but that's only when the game is teaching you the mechanics in the beginning. Later on it gets demanding and expects you to master both strategic shooting and bullet dodging.
The main mechanic of the game is sort of a block puzzle. By shooting colored blocks on the backround layer you can push them around. Knock blocks of the same colour into eachother and they explode dealing damage to enemies and bullets. Larger chains deal more damage. If you cancel bullets this way on bosses they take damage. This may sound confusing but the game really shows you through it and in the end the core mechanic is quite simple. The challenge to the player is figuring out how to deal with various situations on the fly. Often times you'll find yourself thinking out when to shoot and figure out a plan while managing your way through bullet curtains. Murasaki encourages you to be smart about your shooting sort of like Ikaruga or old school 80's shmups.
A bullet health system is the other half of the puzzle mechanic. A bullets color matches its health and they are damaged by block explosions or the players shot. It's implemented quite well and makes you choose between shots or the size of block chains to go for. The default character is far better at cancelling bullets (ie. defense) while the other can land bigger attacks off the puzzle blocks. The latter also has to be careful going to the top of its screen as she has little range to shoot downwards. However dont expect to be able to always rely on bullet cancels, on higher health patterns this wont work. Often to get larger block chains for tricky sections you will end up not shooting for extended periods and having to dodge much more.
Murasaki's soundtrack is really amazing, top notch and there's a lot of competition in this genre. The chill music on stages goes well with the puzzle element and boss themes match their intensity. A fair bit of music syncing, especially with the true route of stage 5. Even if you're not a fan of the gameplay itself the music might surprise you.
After getting the ending you unlock the 6th extra stage which is far more challenging than anything preceding it. The boss of this stage truly demands some dodging skills and figuring out the tricks of its patterns. If you're not a shmup veteran this stage will likely be a wall, but smart play is still always rewarded so it can be enjoyable to learn shmups in this way.
The game includes a hard mode for the first 5 stages which makes their difficulty curve match more with the extra stage. The bosses get significantly harder and you need to approach some stage sections more as a puzzle. Stage 6 on normal is still tougher than anything in hard mode. There's also an endless stage that really tests your skill in the puzzle element as you cannot memorize and it keeps on getting tougher.
Definitely one of the best value for money for STG/shmups on Steam unless you have an aversion to bullet cancelling gimmicks. Murasaki implements its idea well and is a joy to play. Should be refreshing to anyone who thinks shmups are out of innovative ideas. It's worth noting this was first released as a free game, and for that it is quite amazing.

This is a certain type of game - love it or leave it.
You can't "win" the game in a hurry, and there's no point.  This is the kind of exercise where if you could press a game and win, you would wonder why you had the game in the first place... that button is the uninstall button, and it will help you stop your struggle.
Otherwise, this game is fun, interesting, and will last you a long time.  Play for a few minutes a day, or more if you want - but it's not that engaging.  It's just not that kind of game.  It's a math exercise, pure and simple.  Decide what to do with your funds every second, or minute or day or week - leave it alone for a week if you want, no one will care.  I've been playing a few minutes a day for several months, and I'm most of the way to the end of the main game.  They've done well adding extra planets and events, but the main game will take literally a year to finish, unless you want to spend money (and sometimes you will!).
Love it or leave it - it's not an FPS, it's a math game.  It's casual and it's forgiving.  If you like that, try it.

To anyone wonderig about this game being an Owerwatch clone; it's not quite.
There are similarities sure, but a clone? Nah.
Things it does different:
-It's a 5v5, not a 6v6
-You can't change a hero during a game
-The healers actually do a lot of damage, and can 1v1 most DPS's
-There are loadouts, cards that you apply to each specific champion, that can drastically change the playstile of that hero
-During a match, you build up currency with wich you can purchase perks (kinda like those MOBA games, you know the ones)
Perks such as Life Rip ( which heals you as you damage the enemy), or Nimble (increases your movement speed)
-There are daily quests, which reward you for playing the game
-It's F2P
And plenty more.
Some positives:
-A large champion pool
-Frequent updates (which includes new champions, maps, and bug fixes). We're talking some
kind of a patch on an almost daily basis
-Runs stable, no FPS drops
-Quests
-Daily rewards system
-F2P, and no P2W
Some cons:
-Hitboxes are obscenely large, which makes the game casual af.
-Maps look kinda meh, and not really that engaging
-Has it's share of bugs
-Graphically nothing impressive (it's not bad, but nod good either), but that's a personal prefference; if you want it to look sharp, crisp, and beautiful, sorry bud. If you don't really care as much, heyy, right on...
Anyway, it's similar to OW in some regards, bur very different in others. I play both, and enjoy both.
It's definitelly worth a look, and it's F2P so you've really nothing to lose.

I want to love this controller. It is durable, comfortable to use, and extremely innovative. The main problem is that it is not currently supported by most games. I understand that this is because it is a brand new piece of hardware, but the default thumbstick/button layout is madness. The small size and low position of the abxy buttons are difficult to get used to for anyone who has used an xbox or playstation controller.
On the upside, the controller is completely remappable, with a staggering amount of customization options. You can also download other players' custom button layouts so you can see how others are finding ways to comfortably play. However building your own control layout can be tedious, and requires a lot of testing to get to a point where using the custom controls feels comfortable.
The custom mappings are currently only available in big picture mode.
I hope that in the future developers will put good use to the dual trackpads, but in its current state i don't find using this controller as fun and easy as I had hoped.

My wife bought me this controller as an early Christmas present, and it has turned out to be everything I have ever wanted a controller to be.
First Glance:
- It feels sturdy and well made, yet not heavy, it is well balanced in that way.
- There is no battery pack, its takes (and includes) 2 AA batteries (Thank you!). I have always hated built in batteries and battery packs, they are just too expensive and a headache to replace, so I was super pumped when I found out it took standard batteries
- It comes with a USB cable that has a mini USB on the other end, and it also comes with an external USB port. There are 2 things you can do here, you can use the cable to plug right into your controller for battery free playing, or you can plug that cable into the external USB port and plug the wireless adapter into that for better wireless reception. Definitely a perk there!
- I have mid sized hands, and everything is comfortable and easy to reach, feels very natural
Customization:
- Here is where this controller really shines, it truly exceeded all my expectations in this department. From customizing key-binds, to choosing when and how the controller vibrates/clicks, there really isn't anything missing for customization
- one of the greatest things here is that the community can save and upload their configuration for this controller for each game for other users to download! Not only that but the controller will automatically use the configuration you chose for a particular game as soon as you start the game up, making this INCREDIBLY hassle free.
*One of my favorite perks of this controller, you can control your main desktop with it as soon as you plug it in. laying in bed browsing youtube from your controller or whatever you like (you can also do this in steam's big picture mode with the controller) is a wonderful perk
Finally, the learning curve, and this is where users will absolutely fall in love with this controller, or dismiss it. Yes this is completely different from the most popular controllers on the market, and yes you are going to need to grasp a feel for it for each game you play, and finally, yes it is far superior to an Xbox or PS controller.
To really make this learning curve as easy of a transition as possible, I recommend going to the community for the particular game you are playing and downloading the top 2 most popular configs for that game and give them both a half hour of testing and pick the one you like best and you can tweak that config from there to better suit you.
My hat's off to you valve, this controller, in my opinion, is a revolutionary design.

After using the Steam Controller for a few weeks I am convinced this is the best controller I have ever purchased. I have primarily been using it to play MMOs from my couch. For games that use keyboard and mouse with a large number of keybinds the controller does remarkably well. Add the Steam Link and the ability to play comfortably on the couch means that I have fallen in love with this controller.
The biggest downside of this controller is that if you were to pick it up and use stock templates for 30 minutes and then review the controller there are goods odds that you would hate it. My biggest suggestion is to give the controller time, look at videos or read guides on tips for setup and invest time into relearning you have learned over the past decade with other controllers.
If you are used to using a Xbox controller and want something that you can easily pickup and play unfortunately this product will not be for you. It takes me a good 15 minutes with every game that I play to setup bindings and adjust the controller to my liking and more time to feel comfortable with what I just setup. After the learning period with new games the ability to play games on this controller that I would never attempt on a standard controller is a fantastic.

I could see how my previous comment could be misread or misjudged so I spruced this review up a bit.
I guess I'll do one of those cliche pro and con reviews with a grade at the end. Also quite a bit has changed from the last time I posted.
PROS
Comfort
Feels great in my hands. When using an a xbox 360 controller I get cramps in my hand especially after playing something like Skyrim or Bioshock for 6 hours. I suspect this is because of the design of the handles. They go upward a bit instead of curving in downward which SOUNDS weird on paper but in practice is very comfy. For guys like me with big hands PS3/4 controllers just do not feel good. People say the Steam Controller feels "cheap" but I imagine them to be small handed girly men, because that is how I feel about PS controllers. I'm just saying though.
Innovative
The d-pad is replaced with a trackpad, but fear not this trackpad can be used like a d-pad and actually feels and looks like a really big d-pad. I've been able to map up to 36 different functions to the trackpad but only for experimentation. In practice the most I use is it as is for anything between a simple wasd "emulator" to a quick way to access my favorites or weapons lists. For example, mapping weapon hotkeys makes the trackpad so useful especially knowing you can enter several different commands (that are all binded simultaneously, by my choice) by actually pressing the directions, hovering and choosing from a menu that pops up, and move by "gliding" your thumb across it.
Accessibility
You feel like jumping into a game, and not spending hours binding keys, because 1 you feel lazy and full and 2 you don't even know the keys for the game you just purchased? No problem. I've only come across one game that did not have any premade templates from the devs or a community made binding/template. Plus there are templates for rpgs, fps, platformers, etc. This really doesent require a lot of work, but if you want to spend a lot of time binding and customizing you can.
Reliability
Yes it uses double a batteries instead of a charge function, but this is a good thing. I mean really, have you ever charged anything on your PC? Like a phone? It takes FOREVER. The good thing about the battery usage is that it takes like a month for the battery charge on the SC to drop. Even with persistent play. There is also a usb you can use if you lack the foresight to keep spare batteries near your pc. Rechargeable double a batteries are also an option. Get two pairs so you always have a charged set. The battery compartment is pretty wicked too. IDK how to explain it it's just really cool. Also I've "dropped" mine across the room many times playing CS and it still looks and works like new.
Customization
Do I really have to explain this one. You can customize almost everything with this controller, you can even use it as a mouse for your PC and type with it.
Dual Wielding
You can actually use the keyboard in conjunction with the SC, at your leisure and convinience, cool right?
Community
The community has gotten a lot better now that the scrubs and neigh sayers have either learned how to use the darn thing or moved on. Alot of people bought the SC thinking it was going to be the Xbox One Elite controller, and it's not. I see that as a good thing. Some people are angry about that. Whatever. We are constantly working on new bindings together and improving on eachothers templates for specific games and even genres. It's really fun. I've made a few friends just from updating their bindings or vice versa. It's almost like a game within itself.
Cons
Variety
Only one color, black. I like it personally but I suspect people want their neon green and hot pink controllers. Also there are currently no versions made by Mad Catz and other controller companies but that is something that is probably already in the works. I would love to see an Alien Ware SC.
Effectiveness is reduced to genre and even sub genre.
Obviously you cannot use this for games that use tons of keys, at least not without making some sacrifices. Some games are just meant to be played on the mouse and keyboard. MOBAS and competitive FPS games like Counter Strike do not pair well with the SC. It can be done, especially when features like gyroscope are implemented but I find myself using this for single player and certain co op games. Bioschock, Left 4 Dead 2, Skyrim and Fallout are great examples. This is perfect for those types of games when you want to lay back in your bed or on your couch without setting up a mouse and keyboard on your belly. But you want to WIN games on CSGO? Stick to the keyboard, bud.
No rate/review system for community bindings.
This can be a problem, luckily there arent many if any trolls posting stuff that makes you alt tab out of your game everytime you pull the trigger, but the possibility lurks and it is frightening. Also, some people have no idea what they are doing OR they change things and forget to alter their description. Also the description is very hard to edit for some reason, probably because the SC is on and for whatever reason its hard to use the SC and keyboard at the same time in the menu but during an actual game this problem ceases to exist. Weird I know. The best we have right now is a popularity scale, but remember, the most popular is not always the best. And usually isn't.
Big picture mode is still buggy
While SC does not require BPM to run, it is still a cool feature that would be nice if the darn thing were not so buggy. Sometimes I'm playing a game and decide to alter the bindings a bit. So I'll press the steam icon to bring up BPM and for whatever reason it does not appear. OR it will appear, but "under" my game. Meaning I will sometimes have to alt tab out just to get to big picture mode. There is also a weird bug where the joystick refuses to work from time to time but it is forced by turning the controller off and back on. Unfortunately you have to press the steam icon and go into BPM to do this and the other thing happens and it requires a full alt tab out which can result in some unpleasantness and freezing. These bugs mostly happen on lower end PCs but can occasionally even happen on my brand new beast machine, so... Just be mindful of that. It's a small nuisance but a nuiscance none the less.
Neutral
Price
$50 which is $10 cheaper than it's competitors. Some say it feels cheap but that is subjective because I think it feels comfy and sturdy which is a hard feat to master.
Appearance
I think it looks cool although some people tell me it looks dorky. Everyone loves the backpaddles though. And no one can deny the powers of the gyro.
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Grade: B+
I would of gave it an A had the bugs with BPM and the internal software of the SC been fixed in recent updates but because of that I have to knock it down. I gotta knock it down another notch because of the lack of foresight that the SC would create a community. It would be really helpful to have that rate and review system in place. When and if these things are fixed I would change my grade. Game informer gave it a C-. We all know GI if for 12 year olds.....

Second the Controls and Choices: The controls were well implemented, and I like I can use a controller. This game is ♥♥♥♥ing pathetic.
My name is TheMattyXz
and I was one of the first to ever play this game in his "Unity" version (the one made by Zeb89 and some spanish coder).  Game was awful then, is still awful now.
Where do I begin?
First of all, a bit of history. The old game was a mess, badly coded, poorly optimized and had HUGE security holes (needless to say that a bunch of scriptkiddies was able to hack into the game login system in a matter of days). Gameplay was unacceptable and overall the game is a failure.
So, what changed? This new version must be good right?
Well, other than the engine change (from Unity to UE3) and the fact that instead of the spanish coder now we have some underage kid, nothing much has changed.
Game is still pretty much unplayable. I've had the "pleasure" of doing three matches with your average players in your average public server, and nothing was right.
Down to the movements, which in an arena are pretty important. The character is laggy, movements are imprecise and bhopping or any sort of articulate movement is unexistant.
Even by spectating and looking at other players you can see how bad the animations are (idling and moving are way too similar).
The sound? I'll just say this: If you stand still and tap very quickly you'll hear the running sound (which, by the way, is IDENTICAL across every floor material) even though you barely made a step - this means that in the game code there's only one sound for movement and that is "run", even if you just make a small step, the running sound will play. Wow.
Now to gameplay. While I hold my laughter, let me tell you that HALF of the weapons are absolutely useless. The lightning gun emits a weak pathetic laser that barely hits, the pistol looks like a toy and deals little to no damage, the main shotgun is way too weak, and  the cymbal-saw thingies are a good idea but not really well implemented, since the bouncing of walls is broken and the projectiles rarely hit the player.
Rocket launcher is overpowered, as usual in those cheaply-made arenas. The double shotgun is okay and so is the lmg, but that's about it, really.
Respawning happens literally in two places, and spawncamping is way too easy as far as I've seen.
Now, the biggest issue with this game is jumping in my opinion. Especially the jumping platforms, those are so badly made it's almost impossible to explain. It's just funny to see people trying to reach and climb the platform while jumping on these things, it usually takes 4-5 attemps and usually out of boredom people start shooting themselves in those platforms instead of trying to jump and grab the items.
There are also other minor issues, such as the fact that with my computer (Intel Core i7 5930K, GTX980Ti, 16GB DDR4, SSD Raid0) I can barely score 100fps in 2560x1600, whereas in MUCH MUCH bigger games with even better graphics (UT4 comes to mind, which is also free...)  I can score more than 200fps steadily.
Bummer, thank god I got this free because I had the old version.
What's wrong with this game overall? The coders are incompetent, the game is a trainwreck and I don't expect this to go anywhere, as I've seen it fail once already.
PLEASE, DON'T BUY THIS. GET UT4 AND HAVE A SUPERIOR ARENA EXPERIENCE. IT'S ALSO FREE!
And if you really want to spend 20€/$ on Steam, please get a better game, you won't regret NOT playing this.

I have a massive nostalgia hard-on for the series them being my first love in videogaming ever (when I was like 10 or so) so I might probably not be able to be really neutral on this review. Regardless, I will try and number the pros and cons of the game itself:
- Silly story, silly dialogue. Very in-line with any other Lucasarts titles, Simon the Sorcerer, Teen Agent or the like. Harmless, witty and a bit meta sometimes. The kind of humor the Deponia guys have been trying (and failing) so hard to convey in their games.
- Gameplay is what you would expect from a SCUMM game. Pure point and click, with some overworld map sections. Old and new versions use their own inventory and action systems, and I'll get into each one further on. Most of the game consists of going places, talking to people picking up stuff and using it on other stuff to advance further on in the story. At one point one will be required to master insult swordfighting, which is kind of a minigame that to me felt fun to do but that I could see some people seeing like a chore. It's fortunately not super long and it pretty much plays itself so it's not a big deal.
- Although some puzzles are certainly random and cryptic, overall most times the solution to a problem will be hinted at by the game. You can't die*, you won't run out of time, the game will save you a lot of backtracking by skipping some of it, and there is not a lot that you won't be able to solve with some patience in last instance. There is also a hints system in the Special Edition, but I couldn't use it. I'll touch on that further on.
*
- Music is great. Not only the main theme is one of the most iconic and memorable songs in all of videogaming for a reason, the whole OST is made of catchy pirate-caribbean-y songs. Personally I prefer the MIDI versions over the newer instrumentals. Probably nostalgia, see above.
Now, I have vastly differing opinions regarding graphics, GUI and voices. This happens because Monkey Island Special Edition can be played in two ways that for me radically change how the game plays, and that kinda ruin each separate mode for me.
Regarding voices, my problem is, very simply put, you can't play classic mode with voiceovers. Which absolutely baffles me considering not only that Monkey Island 2 SE already had that out of the box, but that also you can actually fix yourself a classic version with voiceovers using
, so that gives no excuse as to why Lucasarts couldn't have patched this at some point. That kinda ruins Classic mode for me and made me feel kinda ripped off when I bought this before I found out about this third party workaround.
Interface wise I guess it comes down more to personal opinion. I prefer the old SCUMM GUI where you had the array of actions and items on the bottom, and I think there's a good reason it was the standard on a ton of point and clicks of the 90s. I personally don't feel like I need to sacrifice the nimbleness of that system for collapsible inventories and contextual stuff like Sam & Max Hit the Road or this game's "remake" mode do just to see more of the screen honestly. So that's a yay for classic mode, nay for the remake. Regarding the hints system I thought it was a nice addition, but due to me having to play the game on scummvm using that patch above to be able to play Classic with voiceovers, I didn't have the chance to use it.
Now: the graphics. Hoo boy.
First off, let me say: I am aware the classic mode looks chunky as hell. I am aware that the new graphics do look very detailed and very in line with the series' aesthetics after it hit 3. The problem comes from how absolutely disconnected everything feels. Talking animations are, no joking, 2 frames, while people actually look like they are talking in classic mode. And it's not just the animation, but the fact that the newer models usually don't seem to look at each other while talking, instead just looking into the distance. A lot of the background does look nicer, yes, but the scaling is jarring as *hell* on the new graphics, while the pixely nature of the classic mode helps a lot with that. And honestly, getting into the models themselves, I personally prefer the more natural, regular dude kinda feel the old graphics have to the humongous bobbleheads that while detailed, sometimes feel like watching a bunch of animatronics.
Regarding the graphics especially it's really heartbreaking to have seen Lucasarts in its final years pouring so much money and talent into remastering one of their pivotal adventure games and coming out with something that's so pretty yet so unpleasant and so unpractical. Especially when you compare it to the more-than-15-years-old Monkey Island 3, which in my opinion hit right all the notes this remaster does wrong.
So. As a product, out of the box, I don't think this is a very good game. Given that both versions have different features that could be cross-compatible, it would have been good to see more customization in that aspect, especially regarding voiceovers. I have huge problems with the remastered version's graphics, and overall I would recommend going
and playing classic with voiceovers.
That said, this is a very fun, long, memorable, silly and entertaining adventure with great voicework. If you're looking to get into the big point and clickers of the 90s, or if you're looking for the definitive version of this game, absolutely pick it up. Price is very reasonable, especially on bundle.
9/10 for the game itself, 8/10 for the SE edition.

The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition is a remake of the popular Lucas Art point and click adventure game which was released back in 1990. The remake was released in mid-2009 on PC, Mac, PSN and Xbox Live Arcade. The game is set in the Caribbean at the time of pirates. You play as Guy Threepwood - a guy who dreams of becoming a pirate.
This game is set in a third person perspective point and click style gameplay. You are able to explore around the world and interact with objects in a couple of different ways, such as inspecting them, picking them up, pushing or pulling for example, whilst you are also able to interact with other NPCs in the game through multiple dialogue options. The game has no death scenes in it for your character; game play is heavily focused on puzzles and exploring. The puzzles in The Secret of Monkey Island are in adventure style; and make no sense what so ever until you finally figure it out, then it becomes clear as day, but all of the puzzles are fun to take part in. Personally my favourite would be the pirate insulting duels. This was the first game in a long while that actually had me taking notes on a pen and paper! None of the puzzles are really time based, so you can spend as much time as you want on them without being penalized.
What I really liked about The Secret of Monkey Island is that you can either play the game in the remastered settings with the higher quality art style, or you can actually play it in the classic pixel style that the original game was based on, you can do this on a scene by scene basis too.  The art style of the remastered edition looks really good though, lots of vibrant colours and some really nice looking background environments.
As this was my first experience with The Secret of Monkey Island I wasn't sure what to expect from it story wise, but I was pleasantly surprised when there is a whole load of humour added into the plot. Every single character I ran into had an extremely memorable persona. I don't want to spoil any of the story since the game is essentially the story, but it is captivating and interesting right until the end.
The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition is completely voice acted, and done really well. Even the none main characters are voice acted, such as bar dwellers and town folk which was a nice touch, much of the sound track is also the same, just remastered to a higher quality.
This is another game that completely baffled me at parts, whether it be on some of the puzzles or just knowing where to go next to progress the story; which resulted in me looking up the guide, to be honest I am not sure how you are supposed to figure some of it but it has been done by plenty of others! I was really immersed in the story of the game and didn't want to lose too much time faffing around with not knowing where to go so I was happy to look up the answers this time.
Each of the game's scenes has plenty of objects that you can interact with, most will end up with Guy giving some sort of witty remark towards them, and there are also lots of NPCs which you can talk with to get more out of the plot and some of the side stories going off in the game too.
The Secret of Monkey Island took me ten hours to complete; this was with the aid of a guide at parts, and following up all dialog options with NPCs to get the most out of the lore; I thought this was a pretty good length for the game considering I actually thought it would be a lot shorter given my past experience of point and click games. Given that the story is linear and that there is only one ending to the game, there is no reason to replay it through a second time though.
Given that this is a remastered edition of the game, it works fine on the newer operating systems, and I was able to play at 4K resolutions perfectly fine. I encountered minor problems with the controls in the game, and the scroll wheel functionality when choosing which action to take on objects stopping randomly - but this was easily worked around by using the keyboard shortcuts.  An odd issue which has been reported is that for some reason the game refuses to run when being installed on a 3 TB hard drive, so that may be something to consider if you are purchasing it and you only have a 3 TB drive.
The Secret of Monkey Island is often referred to as the pinnacle of point and click adventure games, and this series is what spawned many more of the greats we have today, and rightly so. I thoroughly enjoyed every moment of my time playing this game, and the story is absolutely brilliant and I cannot wait to get stuck into the rest of the series. The low price of £6, 99 on Steam makes The Secret of Monkey Island: Special Edition a serious contender for a must play title.

This game is very unique. If I had to give an analagous comparison, I'd say it'd be the lovechild between a single-player Phantasmagoria of Flower View and Air Hockey. If that made absolutely no sense, then continue reading.
This game has several stages you can choose from, and only one fixed difficulty. Completing a stage unlocks the next stage, and you can play any stage at will. The first stage is a low-key tutorial with passive messages explaining the game's mechanics, but it's not a tutorial stage; it's the first stage. The controls are very simple; use the directional keys to move, one button to shoot, and another button to charge up your 'bomb' which clears many bullets around you. These controls, as well as the game's resolution (options limited to 160x120, 320x240, 640x480, 800x600, and 1280x960) and fullscreen/windowed settings can be changed in the config menu option upon startup, but cannot be changed in-game.
Gameplay consists of maneuvering your character through whatever bullets may be present and firing your one shot straight forward. Yes, one; you can only have one shot on screen at a time, but it's not nearly as bad as it sounds. Your shot removes whatever bullets it hits along its path and disappears once it rebounds off the other side and goes through the bottom of the screen. The objective is to shoot the frequently spawning red and blue shapes which, when shot, will move in the direction you shot them and explode after a short time, doing damage to enemies and clearing bullets in a set radius. If you shoot a shape into another shape of the same color, it will cause a chain explosion, clearing even more bullets and doing more damage. Because your standard shot does very little damage on its own, boss battles are a constant battle of positioning, spacing, and carefully shooting the shapes into clusters of bullets, clearing them off the screen and subsequently damaging the boss.
In conclusion, this game's alright. It's very unique and feels weird at first, but doesn't take too long to get used to. Because your character has a health bar (that can be replenished if you do a super awesome chain reaction explosion), if you get hit with several bullets, it's not an instant game-over unlike several other danmaku games I've played. So this game is Murasaki, a puzzle/shmup hybrid by Katetama, most famous for the freeware puzzle/horror game Irisu Syndrome. If you played a bit of that, you should be somewhat familiar with the mechanics in this game, at least the puzzle parts anyway.
It's different from typical SHMUPs in that your bullet isn't really used to destroy the enemies. It has a low rate of fire, terrible range and won't really do much to anything but the most basic of enemies.
What your bullet CAN do however, is hit upon little geometrical shapes, "pucks" of sorts throughout the stage and when they are hit, they explode, taking along any bullets and enemies within its blast radius. Where it gets really interesting is when you make these shapes hit each other in a chain reaction and cause massive screen wiping explosions. Therein lies the real fun of Murasaki, the defining gimmick of this SHMUP.  You hold out for as long as you can against cascading waves of bullets from all directions, slowly waiting for the shapes to pile up, and when the moment is right, you just fire one bullet to start off the chain reaction and watch everything blow away to void as you rack up a massive score.
It's a very satisfying and adrenaline pumping experience, one wholly unique to itself. Other shmups have their own unique methods, but this one is something really interesting.
That's not all this game has to offer though. There is a story in this game, but it's very cryptic and dependent on how well you do in a stage and whether you decide to let the boss characters say their piece instead of firing at them... And from what I can gleam of it from where I'm at so far in the game, it's a tragic story about good intentions leading to horrible circumstances, loss, horrific experiments, incredibly powerful beings destroying everything in their wake for reasons not entirely clear... But in the midst of all this, there's also a promise to be kept and the uniting power of music even after death... And it all happens in the background, never really at the fore, only told in snippets outside of gameplay.  It's odd, but I think it's really good myself.
The music in this game is made with such passion for the themes present in the game that it basically defines moments in the games. The composer understood the the mood of the setting and pulled off a soundtrack that just completely hits all the right spots with aplomb. It's a soundtrack that many games want but often never get. I have nothing but the highest praise for the music  and would recommend the game just for the music alone. Thankfully, the game is also really good too.
There are five stages, an extra stage, an unlockable hard mode (That is REALLY hard), and an endless mode, in addition to various achievements that unlock small portions of the story... This all sums to to saying there's a lot for you to enjoy here for the very low price of entry. You have two characters to play as, each has their own unique feel.
I am not sure if a lot of shmup fans who like traditional styled bullet hell games will like it, but I think all shmup fans should try it out anyway if they can. It's a captivating experience that left an impression on me that I won't soon forget, and I'd want others to play this and maybe feel a little bit of the excitement and wonder I got when I played this. I think it's more than worth the asking price.

Murasaki:
~~~~~~~

How are your reflexes, people? Are they slow, medium or super-fast? The good news for you is, this game will make your reflexes top notch! Are you ready for a fun, fast and challenging bullet hell game? I bet you are. . .  Here it is, welcome to Murasaki!
At the start of the game, you will only be able to play the first of six available stages (the last stage needs to be unlocked). After choosing either Kairi (I recommend this character if you are a novice in this type of game) or Sutsaki, you will start the first level. This stage comes with a small tutorial and will show you what to do with the orange block and blue circles. Remember one important point – only one shot at a time!! There is no rapid fire in this game!  Hit either the orange blocks or the blue circles – they will explode within a few seconds!! Hit them in a certain way so they can travel to the most concentrated area of bullets and clear the zone!
How do the bullets appear? Well, you have several enemies. The most common ones are these funny white thingies with flowers on their heads! They spit bullets in all directions - even in a spiral! You will also have fish flying around and they will leave a trail of bullets, too. In the middle of the stage, you will have something like a mini boss to eliminate and then the last boss of the stage.
The bullets come in different colours; you will have to hit the white ones only once, two shots for the blue and three shots for the yellow. However, you can create a chain reaction if you manage to put an orange block or a blue circle right in the middle of the biggest concentration of bullets.
Pick up blue and red orbs, too. The blue ones will give you back some well-needed health while the red ones will give you access to an additional magic bomb. What is a magic bomb, you may ask? Well, if you are surrounded by a large number of bullets and can’t see how to get out of this peculiar situation, just activate the magic bomb and no more bullets around you - Yeehah!
Nice artworks. The soundtrack is sublime and you can choose either the keyboard or the gamepad for the controls.
Positives:

-	Fast, fun and addictive game
-	Use blocks or circles to create chain reaction
-	Splendid soundtrack
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	I would like to see more stages

Before starting I should mention that I have had more time with this game than my total playtime would indicate as I have played the Japanese version prior to the Steam release.
The game is described as a hybrid shmup/puzzle game- but, I personally feel that it becomes something entirely unique by combining elements of the two. While some skills from other shmups will carry over to this game- if you try to play it too much like a classic shmup then it's easy to quickly be consumed by the onslaught of enemy projectiles.
Rather than firing a constant stream of bullets the player only has a single bullet that can be fired once at a time. This bullet can clear weaker enemy bullets from the screen- but it's mainly used to hit blocks that spawn around the level. By knocking these blocks into each other the player is able to create explosions which can clear the area of bullets and destroy enemies. This means that rather than confront enemies directly the player must use the bullet to set up explosive combos and clear a path before they become overwhelmed.The game is designed in such a way that it's able to retain the high intensity and do-or-die nature of a shmup while also including the intricacy and deliberation of a puzzle game.
Much like the developer, Tetsu’s, other games- this game also features a few secrets and a clever way of presenting the narrative through the design of the game. Combine this with Watson’s amazing music and you end up with an intriguing somber atmosphere that’s difficult to find elsewhere.
If you’re looking for a fresh take on a classic genre then I would highly recommend checking this game out!

Bought it when it was on sale. Would definitely recommend at sale price. Would probably recommend at full price. Basically if you've got the money to spend and are not bothered by anything you see. (if you want to know how long it takes: my total time is how long it took me to finish every route, get every CG & achievement, aaand I nodded off while it was running for almost an hour once.) Anyway. I love dating sims, and overall, I would say I had fun with this one.
Pros:
The storylines are cute, even the routes I liked the least had charming parts. Also I looove Reese's route it was so adorable. My heart melted. (Reese is 100% best boy pls date him.)
Concept is interesting and unique as far as I know, (spoilersbutnotreally): all the characters are under a curse that turns them into cats when they leave the cafe.
Said curse is broken by learning magic, and each character has a unique type of magic that they learn, develop, and then use to beat down the bad guy (well, Hayes and Finley's magic are a bit similar imo. But they're still all cool and impressive).
The characters are pretty neat and most of them are easy to connect to emotionally. I even felt for Nacht a bit at the very end.
Cats are consistently drawn very very cute.
You get to choose pronouns plus a character portrait. Cast is diverse! This is particularly exciting because it is not something you see very frequently in dating sims or VNs.
Overall I'd say it has the makings of a pretty solid dating sim-type VN. And it feels like it was made with love!
Cons (I'm nitpicky, sorry. There's a lot here but I still enjoyed the game overall and would recommend. Well, unless there's anything here that's a dealbreaker for you.):
Storylines are almost the exact same until about the halfway point no matter whose route you're on, which can get boring, especially because the skip option is rather slow and doesn't work if the window isn't at the front (for me, anyway).
Art for some characters looks a bit inconsistent between some of their portraits and CGs. And while probably most of the art looks pretty nice, some looks rather unfinished.
You can't change the character's name, and the differences between the feminine/masculine portraits for Avery aren't there a lot of the time (in almost all of the CGs the only difference at all is the hairstyle.) And the more feminine portrait's body type is basically just very skinny and slightly femme but mostly androgynous. If you like that, more power to you. But it's not super often I get to play as a girl who looks like me (see: brown) in a dating sim/VN so I wish I could've had a body that was more accurate too.
Also, Avery in general I didn't find terribly likeable or relatable. Mason's route had me cringing at points (even though I found the reconciliation very touching), along with some of the Hayes interactions (I have very bad anxiety myself, and helping him do the dishes and that time where Avery says something about Hayes not liking them anymore as a joke and Hayes gives a startled/embarrassed just rubbed me the wrong way it felt insensitive lol).
Last and definitely least important: I think the theme song is annoying.

Before I start this review I would like to say that I am a hardcore fan for the Dead Rising franchise.
This game, WOW. I love this game, it has been getting bad reviews for the bad optimisation  and crashes, but I have had no crashed what so ever throughout playing 5 hour straight sessions on this game. With the optimisation (yes the game is capped at 30fps), I am OCD when it comes to FPS, I have to have it a 60+, when I first started playing the game I felt the 30fps and was like urrgh, but once you start getting into the game you can't even tell it's on 30.
Okay, down to gameplay.
Dead Rising 3 brings new custom weapons and an all new custom vehicles to the game. Capcom have really made a difference to the new Dead Rising, instead of adding a couple of customs, like Dead Rising OTR. The all new open world in los perdidos, is amazing. The diffrence between Fortune City and this City is huge. No more loading screens to enter a certain casino, you can just run and no loading screens will make you sit there waiting. I think this was a major let down for the other Dead Rising games which CapCom did a brill job of fixing.
They have still got the old school customs, such as the knife gloves, electric rake, etc, but they have added many more, that much more that you will rarely find a custom which was in the previous games. They have also added all new collectables, such as the Frank West collectables, scattered across the map, when you find them you will be rewarded PP points. They have also added the tragic deaths. Which are bodies scattered around the map, which have a upsetting feeling once you find them. I get the goosebumps when the music and the message appear, I think this is one of the best features to Dead Rising 3 and I say well done to you guys at Capcom!
They have also added the new survivor feature, back in Dead Rising 2, you helped survivors, then you take them to the safe house and that's it, you can't keep them to assist you in the zombie infested city, but in Dead Rising 3, once you help survivors, you can dismiss them and then get them back out again. This can be done at the safe houses which are scattered around the map. The have also added (again a safe house feature) where you can take out weapons from the storage which are weapons you have collected over time, you have a limit to how much you can take out, once you have ran out of your limit, it regens over time. In my opinion this is not the best idea, but it's a ok-ish feature. I wouldn't of put it in.
Now down to the graphics, they are good. For big open world zombie game, where there are thousands of zombies you can see at once from certain points. They are not the best, granted, but they are good enough for me.
Gameplay - 10/10
Graphics - 9/10
Sound/Music - 10/10
Is this game worth it?
Of course it is.
Thanks Capcom for making an amazing game and bringing it to PC.

I love a good puzzle-platform game and OTS is more than just that. Aside from teleport gun puzzles and platforming navigation throughout the game, you have a story line that ends with a punch-line (a duh moment). The game is highly entertaining to play and I enjoyed playing it the first walkthrough blind. Now that I have completed the game once, the achievements keep the game with a tiny level of replay value. Some are definitely harder to complete because of how the game is designed (backtracking/forgetting something). However, you get to have 3 save-slots so you can take your time and have different slots saved to perform different acheivement as you complete one before the other. Or you can just use the guides present in the community if you aren't into hardcore solve everything by yourself :D.
The game design is mostly simplistic and the different mechanics makes the game enjoyable to master as you progress through the game. You will definitely see the game differently if you've played it once and play it again. The graphics aren't what you call the best, but this is a 2D game. For a 2D game with these graphics, it's definitely on the higher-end imo. The gauss gun is there as a way to kill your enemies, but I definitely enjoyed the game more via the teleport gun because of the puzzles.
Overall, highly recommend this game to people that likes a puzzle-platform game that has a little more and can be played relatively quickly. I finished it in a little over 1 hr by playing leisurely. One of the achievement is to finish the game in 20 mins so this would definitely be a short game. 8.5/10!
